See what they write on antecedent and consequent love, Hague Colloquy p. 183 (Bertius).

source_text: Arg. 3. Beneplacitum Dei de salute humana est ipsa praedestinatio ad salutem: Credentes velle salvare, est beneplacitum Dei de salute hominum: Ergo. Majorem dicunt esse perspicue veram, quia ipsa vox electionis nihil aliud significat, quam Dei beneplacitum de salute hominis electi. Minorem in ipsis verbis Apostoli fundatam ostendunt, 1 Cor. i. 21, Placuit Deo per stultam praedicationem servare credentes. Quod etiam a contrario illustrant, Quia Deus in hominibus minime credentibus non habet beneplacitum, sed anima ejus fastidit eos; juratque tales non ingressuros in requiem suam, 1 Cor. x. 5. Heb. iii. 18.
english: Arg. 3. God's good pleasure concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation; to will to save believers is that good pleasure concerning men's salvation; therefore. They call the Major clearly true, because election means nothing but God's good pleasure concerning the elect man's salvation. The Minor they found in 1 Cor. 1:21 — It pleased God by the foolish preaching to save believers — and illustrate from the contrary: in men who scarcely believe God has no good pleasure, but his soul loathes them, and he swears such will not enter his rest (1 Cor. 10:5; Heb. 3:18).

source_text: Sol. Hoc argumentum idem fere est cum primo, et eodem vitio laborat. Sed iterum respondemus, In majore propositione terminos esse inconcinne et imperite dispositos. Nam Beneplacitum de salute humana est quiddam latius et generalius praedestinatione, debuit itaque praedicati, non subjecti locum occupare, hoc modo; Praedestinatio est Dei beneplacitum de salute humana: Credentes velle salvare est Dei beneplacitum de salute humana: Ergo credentes velle salvare est ipsa praedestinatio. Verum si hoc modo instituta fuisset major propositio, conclusissent ex omnibus affirmativis in secunda figura. Maluerunt itaque praeposteram enunciationem facere, quam manifestam παραλογισμόν committere.
english: Sol. This argument is nearly the same as the first and has the same vice. Again: in the Major the terms are incongruously and unskillfully set. Good pleasure concerning human salvation is wider and more general than predestination, so it ought to be predicate not subject — thus: Predestination is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation; to will to save believers is that good pleasure; therefore to will to save believers is predestination itself. Had they framed the Major that way, they would have concluded from all affirmatives in the second figure. They preferred a preposterous wording to an open fallacy.

source_text: Sed permittamus eos suo modo agere: dico, nisi major propositio sit universalis, ex omnibus particularibus nihil sequetur. Si sit universalis hoc sensu, Quodlibet, vel omne, beneplacitum Dei de salute humana est ipsa praedestinatio ad salutem, tum erit manifeste falsa. Nam in quovis Dei beneplacito de salute humana declarato, non ilico exprimitur aut continetur formale decretum praedestinationis. Declaravit enim Deus in verbo beneplacitum voluntatis suae de qualitatibus et operationibus hominum ad salutem perducendorum, de mediis quibus eos uti oporteat, denique de toto ordine exsequendae praedestinationis: in hisce tamen non continetur electionis decretum, quia ex aequo ad omnes spectant, et per modum legis proponuntur.
english: Let them argue their way: unless the Major is universal, nothing follows from particulars. If universal — Any or every good pleasure of God concerning human salvation is predestination itself to salvation — it is manifestly false. In any declared good pleasure about human salvation the formal decree of predestination is not at once expressed or contained. God has declared in the word his will's good pleasure about the qualities and operations of those to be led to salvation, the means they ought to use, and the whole order of executing predestination — yet those do not contain the election decree, because they look equally to all and are set forth as law.

source_text: Beneplacitum ergo illud in quo ipsa praedestinatio includitur, est aeterna illa et arcana Dei voluntas, qua statuit apud se, ex eadem perditionis massa quasdam personas ex pura misericordia per gratiam efficacem ad gloriam infallibiliter perducere, aliis secundum justitiam in merita perditione relictis.
english: The good pleasure that actually includes predestination is not those declared statutes, but God's eternal secret will: from the same mass of perdition he resolved with himself to lead some persons infallibly to glory by pure mercy through efficacious grace, and according to justice to leave others in the perdition they merit.

source_text: Jam accedo ad Minorem, quae illis Apostoli verbis constat, Credentes velle salvare per stultitiam praedicationis est beneplacitum Dei de salute humana. Quis negat? Est enim beneplacitum Dei de medio et organo, absque quorum ope ad salutem nemo adulta aetate perduci potest. Sed non exprimit illud aeternum εὐδοκίας beneplacitum secundum quod quidam ad salutem et salutis media, praeteritis aliis, eliguntur. Uno verbo; dixit Apostolus, Placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis servare credentes. Requirit igitur praedicationem, et fidem, tanquam media ex Dei beneplacito ad ipsam salutem efficiendam antecedanea. Non dixit, Placuit Deo per stultitiam praedicationis eligere credentes. Non igitur requirit fidem, aut praedicationem, tanquam conditiones praevisas et antecedaneas ad aeternum actum electionis. Neque huc faciunt quae de incredulis ex 1 Cor. x. et ex Hebr. iii. allata fuerunt. Ea enim loca non probant Deum ab aeterno eligere, aut praeterire homines ex antecedanea praevisione fidei aut incredulitatis in iis futurae; sed Deum in exsecutione aeterni sui decreti, tandem introducere eos in requiem suam, quos vocatione efficaci, et secundum propositum operante, reddidit fideles; eos autem excludere, qui proprii cordis corrupta perversitate manent increduli. Cur autem horum potius quam illorum misertus fuerit, noli quaerere, si non vis errare. Sufficiat illud, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero, et commiserabor quem commiseratus fuero, Rom. ix. 15.
english: Now the Minor: to will to save believers by the foolishness of preaching is God's good pleasure concerning human salvation. Who denies it? It is good pleasure about the means and organ without which no adult can be led to salvation. It does not express that eternal εὐδοκία by which some are elected to salvation and its means, others passed by. In a word: the Apostle said It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save believers — so he requires preaching and faith as means antecedent by God's good pleasure to effecting salvation. He did not say to elect believers. So he does not require faith or preaching as foreseen antecedent conditions of the eternal act of election. Nor do 1 Cor. 10 and Heb. 3 on unbelievers help: they do not prove eternal election or passing-by from foresight of future faith or unbelief, but that in executing his eternal decree God finally brings into his rest those whom efficacious vocation working according to purpose has made faithful, and excludes those who remain unbelieving by their own heart's corrupt perversity. Why he had mercy on these rather than those — do not ask, if you would not err. Suffice Rom. 9:15: I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.

source_text: Arg. 4. Aliud argumentum petitur ex Eph. i. 4. Sicut nos elegit in ipso, scil. Christo. Unde sic argumentantur; Electio qua nos elegit in Christo Deus, est tantum credentium: Electio quae facta est ante jacta mundi fundamenta facta est in Christo: Ergo illa credentium tantum est. Majoris veritas ex eo apparet, quod nemo in Christo eligi potest, nisi qui in Christo est, quales sunt soli credentes. Hoc idem argumentum urgitur ab Arminio in Exam. Pred. Perk. pag. 313, 32. ubi haec verba habet, Christus secundum Apostolum, non tantum est medium per quod salus electione jam ante parta obtinetur, sed tanquam causa meritoria, cujus respectu electio facta sit, et propter quem illa gratia sit praeparata. Deus enim neminem ad vitam aeternam amat nisi in Christo: Ex quo sequi videtur, quod cum nemo in Christo consideretur a Deo, nisi ille sit insertus per fidem, Fidelium propria sit electio. Haec ille.
english: Arg. 4. Another argument from Eph. 1:4 — According as he chose us in him, that is Christ. They argue: the election by which God chose us in Christ is of believers only; the election made before the world's foundations was made in Christ; therefore it is of believers only. The Major's truth, they say, is that no one can be elected in Christ unless he is in Christ — and only believers are. Arminius urges the same in Exam. Pred. Perk. pp. 313, 32: on the Apostle, Christ is not only a means through which salvation already gotten by election is obtained, but a meritorious cause in respect of which election is made and for whom that grace is prepared. God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ; so since no one is considered in Christ by God unless inserted by faith, election belongs to the faithful. So he.

source_text: Sol. Ab ipsa conclusione ordiamur responsionem nostram. Dicimus ergo, non concludi illud quod positum est in controversia. Non enim quaeritur utrum electio sit solummodo eorum qui credentes sunt futuri, vel, quod eodem recidit, eorum quos Deus ante jacta mundi fundamenta praevidet credituros; sed utrum aeternus ille actus electionis Divinae praerequirat hanc praevisionem tanquam causam, aut saltem conditionem antecedaneam: quod nos negamus, et adversarii neutiquam possunt probare. Concedimus illis, Electionem esse tantum credentium; sed non credentium in praescientia Divina antecedenter ad ipsam electionem, sed credentium in praescientia Divina consequenter, et virtute gratiae in electione illis praeparatae et destinatae, juxta illud Augustini De Praed. Sanct. cap. 18, Ideo tales eramus futuri quia elegit ipse ut tales per gratiam essemus. Et cap. 10. Praedestinatione Deus praescivit quid fuerat ipse facturus. Consimilia habet cap. 17. Quae loca Augustini si quis consulat, et Arminiani hujus argumenti optimam solutionem, et Paulini hujus contextus optimam explicationem inveniet.
english: Sol. Start from their conclusion: it does not settle what is in controversy. The question is not whether election is only of those who will be believers — or of those God foresaw before the world's foundations would believe — but whether that eternal act of divine election prerequires that foresight as cause, or at least antecedent condition. We deny it; adversaries cannot prove it. We grant election is of believers only — not believers in divine foresight before election, but believers consequently, by virtue of the grace prepared and destined for them in election. So Augustine, De praed. Sanct. 18: we were going to be such because he chose that we should be such through grace; and ch. 10: by predestination God foresaw what he himself would do (likewise ch. 17). Consult those places for the best solution of this Arminian argument and the best reading of this Pauline context.

source_text: Sed missa conclusionis ventilatione accedo ad Majorem; quae fuit hujusmodi, Electio qua nos Deus elegit in Christo est tantum credentium. Si de electione temporali, qua certae personae per vocationem efficacem a mundo improborum secernuntur, intelligatur haec propositio, agnoscimus hanc electionem esse tantum credentium, et actualiter credentium: sed nos de aeterno electionis Divinae actu, non de temporali ejusdem effectu, disputamus. Si ergo hanc aeternam electionem respiciant, quam in hac controversia respicere debent, dicimus hanc electionem non esse credentium, quasi quidam homines extra Christum adhuc constituti praeviderentur a Deo ut credentes, et interveniente hac fide praevisa eligerentur; sed esse credentium, quia Deus praevidit se illis donum fidei daturum, quos in aeterno electionis proposito Christo dare decrevit.
english: Drop the conclusion and take the Major: The election by which God chose us in Christ is of believers only. If that means temporal election — certain persons severed from the wicked world by efficacious vocation — we grant it is of believers, and of actually believing ones. But we dispute the eternal act of divine election, not its temporal effect. So of eternal election (what this controversy must regard): it is not of believers as if men still outside Christ were foreseen as believers and then elected with that foresight intervening; it is of believers because God foresaw he would give the gift of faith to those he decreed in the eternal purpose of election to give to Christ.

source_text: Huc faciunt illa Christi verba apud Johannem vi. 37. Quicquid mihi dat Pater, ad me veniet. Donatio haec aeternam Dei electionem designat: Venire, fidem in humanis cordibus suo tempore productam denotat: a donatio innuitur causa antecedanea veniendi, id est, credendi: non autem fides praevisa causa antecedanea donandi, hoc est, eligendi. Quod autem afferunt ad Majoris confirmationem, Deum non posse illum eligere in Christo qui non est in Christo: Illi autem tantum in Christo sunt, qui a Deo considerantur ut Christo inserti per fidem: ergo soli credentes eliguntur: haec argumentatio nititur falsa expositione illorum verborum Apostolicorum, Elegit nos in Christo.
english: John 6:37 helps here: Whatever the Father gives me will come to me. The donation marks God's eternal election; coming marks faith produced in human hearts in its time. Donation is the antecedent cause of coming (believing) — not foreseen faith the antecedent cause of giving (electing). Their Major confirmation — God cannot elect in Christ one who is not in Christ; only those considered inserted into Christ by faith are in Christ; therefore only believers are elected — rests on a false reading of He chose us in Christ.

source_text: Nam illa verba, in Christo, non ad statum hominis electi, sed ad actum eligentis Dei sunt referenda. Arminiani sic exponunt, Elegit nos in Christo, id est, Nos existentes in Christo, vel nos consideratos et praevisos ut credentes in Christum, et per fidem in illum insertos, Deus postmodum elegit. Sed haec loquendi formula, in Christo, quoties conjungitur cum aliquo actu Divino, non semper innuit subjectum, in quod tendit ille actus, considerari ut existens in Christo antecedenter. Verbi causa, Eph. i. 3. Deus benedixit nobis omni benedictione spirituali in Christo. At inter spirituales benedictiones est ipsa prima fidei et poenitentiae donatio, quae non dantur existentibus in Christo, sed alienis a Christo, ut ad Christum adducantur, et ei inserantur. Sic Deus dicitur in Christo mundum sibi reconciliasse, 2 Cor. v. 19; in Christo ad bona opera nos condidisse, Eph. ii. 10. Denique ipsi Remonstrantes docent Deum regenerare homines in Christo, Coll. pag. 99. In hisce omnibus locis verba illa, in Christo, non possunt nisi absurdissime exponi, in Christo antecedenter existentes. Eligere igitur in Christo nil aliud est, quam in eligendo respicere ad Christum Mediatorem et Caput Ecclesiae, ejusque gratia membra illi conjungenda et glorificanda destinare.
english: In Christ refers not to the elect man's state but to the electing God's act. Arminians expose He chose us in Christ as: us already existing in Christ, or foreseen as believing and inserted by faith, whom God then chose. But in Christ joined to a divine act does not always mean the subject already exists in Christ beforehand. Eph. 1:3: God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ — and among those blessings is the first gift of faith and repentance, given not to those already in Christ but to those alien from him, to bring them to Christ and insert them. So God in Christ reconciled the world to himself (2 Cor. 5:19) and created us unto good works (Eph. 2:10). Remonstrants themselves say God regenerates men in Christ (Coll. p. 99). In all these, in Christ cannot without absurdity mean already existing in Christ beforehand. So to elect in Christ is nothing but, in electing, to look to Christ the Mediator and Head of the Church, and by his grace to destine members to be joined to him and glorified.

source_text: Quod autem Arminius urget, Deum neminem amare ad vitam aeternam nisi in Christo, hoc est, ut ille interpretatur, nisi consideratum ut fidelem, et jam Christo insertum, ac proinde neminem eligere nisi qua fidelem; id de ipsa introductione ad vitam aeternam verum est, sed de praedestinatione falsum. Nam Deus illos omnes hoc sensu ad vitam aeternam amat, quos Christo vivificandos et servandos ante jacta mundi fundamenta dare decrevit. Hi autem qui dantur vivificandi, non considerantur a Deo ut vivificati et fideles, sed ut in peccatis mortui et adhuc infideles. Ut absolvam verbo; Deus dicitur nos elegisse in Christo, non quia consideravit nos tanquam per fidem nostram in Christo existentes, antequam eligeremur, sed quia cum respectu ad Christum Mediatorem ad vitam aeternam praedestinantur quotquot praedestinantur.
english: Arminius urges that God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ — as he reads it, except considered faithful and already inserted into Christ, and so elects none except as faithful. That is true of the introduction itself to eternal life, false of predestination. In that sense God loves to eternal life all he decreed before the world's foundations to give to Christ to be made alive and saved. Those given to be made alive are not considered already made alive and faithful, but dead in sins and still unbelieving. In a word: God chose us in Christ not because he viewed us as already in Christ by our faith before election, but because with respect to Christ the Mediator all who are predestinated are predestinated to eternal life.

source_text: Arg. 5. Quos Deus destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν per Jesum Christum, quosque in Christo tanquam dilecto acceptos, ii considerantur ut fideles: Sed omnes quos Deus elegit ad salutem, teste Eph. i. 5, 6, destinavit εἰς υἱοθεσίαν per Christum, eosque in Christo tanquam in dilecto gratos facit: Ergo omnes quos elegit ad salutem consideravit ut fideles. Major ex eo probatur, quod nulla est adoptio in filios nisi per fidem, Joh. i. 12, Quotquot eum acceperunt; et Gal. iii. 26, Omnes enim filii estis Dei per fidem in Christo.
english: Arg. 5. Their syllogism: those destined unto adoption through Jesus Christ and accepted in Christ as the beloved count as faithful; but Eph. 1:5–6 shows that everyone God elects to salvation he so destines unto adoption through Christ and makes acceptable in the beloved; therefore everyone he elects he considered faithful. They prove the Major from John 1:12 and Gal. 3:26 — no adoption into sons except through faith; you are all sons of God through faith in Christ.

source_text: Sol. Major propositio falsa est. Nam quamvis perfecta adoptio temporalis involvat fidem, ut conditionem antecedentem, vel saltem in ipso momento adoptionis concurrentem; ac proinde nemo considerari possit ut actu adoptatus, qui non simul consideretur ut fidelis: tamen adoptio, vel destinatio εἰς υἱοθεσίαν in mente Divina ante jacta mundi fundamenta considerari et potest, et debet, absque consideratione fidei in nobis tanquam conditionis antecedaneae.
english: Sol. That Major fails. Yes, finished temporal adoption carries faith with it — beforehand as a condition, or at least together with adoption in the same moment — so you cannot treat someone as actually adopted without treating him as faithful. But destination unto adoption in God's mind before the world's foundations can and must be thought without treating our faith as an antecedent condition.

source_text: Nec facit quicquam ad confirmationem Majoris, quod nulla est adoptio in filios, nisi per fidem. Nam licet nulla sit adoptio nisi per fidem, est tamen aeterna destinatio certarum personarum εἰς υἱοθεσίαν, κατὰ τὴν εὐδοκίαν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Eph. i. 5. et non secundum praevisionem fidei nostrae.
english: And it does the Major no good to say there is no sonship-adoption except through faith. Grant the point: there is still an eternal destination of certain persons unto adoption according to the good pleasure of his will (Eph. 1:5), not according to foresight of our faith.

source_text: Nam fides credentium, qua distinguuntur a non credentibus, non consideratur ut antecedaneum hujus Divinae εὐδοκίας, sed effectum, Matth. xi. 26. Videndus est Augustinus De Praedestinatione Sanctorum cap. 13. et 19. Ubi accurate explicat haec ipsa verba Paulina quae urgentur a Remonstrantibus.
english: Believers' faith — what sets them off from unbelievers — is not an antecedent of this divine good pleasure but its effect (Matt. 11:26). Augustine's De praedestinatione sanctorum 13 and 19 carefully opens these very Pauline words the Remonstrants press.

source_text: Sol. (cont.) Augustinus fere hoc caput primum ad Ephesios explicando percurrit. Apponam solummodo haec paucula. Electionem quam significavit Dominus dicens, Non vos me elegistis, sed ego vos elegi; nec fides ipsa praecedit. Non enim quia credidimus, sed ut credamus elegit nos, ne priores eum elegisse dicamur. Periculoso igitur errore confundunt destinatam adoptionem in aeterno actu electionis Divinae cum perfecta adoptione in temporali effectu vocationis efficacis.
english: Sol. (cont.) Augustine nearly walks this first chapter of Ephesians in explaining it. Only a few notes: the election the Lord meant by You did not choose me, but I chose you — and faith itself does not come first. He chose us not because we believed, but that we may believe, lest we be said to have chosen him first. So they dangerously confuse destined adoption in the eternal act of divine election with finished adoption in the temporal effect of efficacious vocation.

source_text: Praecedat fides, aut comitetur saltem adoptionem in ipsis electis peractam: at non potest (vel secundum nostrum considerandi modum) praecedere adoptionem in mente Dei eligentis ab aeterno certis personis decretam et destinatam. Nam fidem salutiferam praecedit vocatio efficax, vel secundum propositum; talem vocationem antecedit praedestinatio sive electio ad gloriam: unde clarum est, non considerari ullos aut praevideri tanquam fideles nisi ex antecedente praedestinationis decreto, quia efficax vocatio, vera fides, et realis adoptio inde dimanat.
english: Faith may precede or at least go with adoption finished in the elect themselves — but it cannot (even on our way of thinking) precede the adoption God from eternity decreed and destined for certain persons in his electing mind. Efficacious vocation according to purpose precedes saving faith; predestination or election to glory precedes that vocation. So none are considered or foreseen as faithful except from the antecedent predestination decree — because efficacious vocation, true faith, and real adoption flow from it.

source_text: Porro, quod dicunt, Deum neminem in Christo gratum facere aut habere nisi fidelem, id nullo modo potest consistere. Quaero enim, Unde nascitur efficax propositum in Deo, inspirandi fidem salutiferam et poenitentiam cordibus humanis? In hoc ipso proposito quod spectat adhuc infideles et impoenitentes, singularem ac specialem quendam Dei amorem agnoscant est necesse. Tantus enim est Dei amor erga Filium suum unigenitum, ut ejus intuitu amore aeternae benevolentiae complectatur eos omnes, quos in illo elegit, etiam in statu peccati et infidelitatis consideratos; et propterea speciali quadam gratia curat semper eos ex hoc statu eruendos. Praeclare in hanc sententiam Concilium Arausicanum, Displicentes amati sumus, ut fieret in nobis unde placeremus, can. 25. Hisce adde, Christum esse caput tam infinitae potentiae, ejusque meritum tantae efficaciae, ut influere possit in membra nondum unita, sed solummodo destinata, et suo influxu efficere ut talia uniantur. Hoc illud est quod Scotus bene observavit, lib. 3. dist. 19. Christus meruit ut non conjuncta sibi conjungerentur: et in hoc potissimum consistit meritum ejus. Si Christi meritum ad non-conjunctos, hoc est, non-credentes, pertingit, efficitque ut conjungantur, tum etiam et conformis quaedam Dei acceptatio sive gratificatio ad eosdem extenditur. Brevius itaque respondeo, Hominem aliquem dici posse Deo acceptum in Christo, vel propter Christum, dupliciter. Uno modo, quando illum complectitur amore quasi praesentis amicitiae, illumque ut domesticum ad thronum gratiae admittit, atque sensu favoris sui beat. Hoc sensu soli fideles sunt in Christo Deo grati. Alio modo intelligi potest aliquis esse prae aliis Deo gratus et acceptus, nimirum, quando illum complectitur amore aeternae benevolentiae, ut praedestinatum Filii sui membrum. Licet enim adhuc paterni amoris effecta ad talem non defundantur, intendit tamen in Christo et propter Christum idoneo tempore diffundere. Et hoc sensu Deus multos etiam nondum credentes et conversos gratos sibi fecit in Christo, non tanquam jam positos in Christo, sed tanquam ex speciali favore ponendos, quia ab aeterno in Christo electos.
english: Further: their claim that God makes or holds none pleasing in Christ except the faithful cannot stand. Whence comes God's efficacious purpose to inspire saving faith and repentance into human hearts? That purpose still regards unbelievers and the impenitent — so they must grant a singular, special love of God there. So great is his love for his only-begotten Son that, looking to him in eternal benevolence, he embraces all he elected in him even while considered in sin and unbelief — and by special grace always works to draw them out of that state. So Orange can. 25: Displeasing we were loved, that there might be made in us whence we might please. Add: Christ is a head of infinite power, his merit of such efficacy that it can influence members not yet united but only destined, and by that influence unite them. Scotus (3 dist. 19) well noted: Christ merited that the not-yet-joined be joined — and therein his merit chiefly consists. If his merit reaches non-believers and joins them, a conforming divine acceptance extends to them too. Briefly: one may be acceptable to God in Christ, or for Christ's sake, two ways. One: present friendship-love, admitted as a household member to the throne of grace — in that sense only the faithful are pleasing in Christ. Two: eternal benevolence as a predestinated member of his Son — though paternal effects are not yet poured out, he intends in Christ and for Christ to pour them at the fit time. In that sense God has made many not yet believing or converted pleasing in Christ — not as already placed in him, but as to be placed by special favor, because elected in Christ from eternity.

source_text: De Minore, quae expressis Scripturae verbis continetur, non opus est aliquid dicam: ex dictis enim facile intelligatur, inde non posse probari, fidem in electione debere considerari ut conditionem praevisam, et electionis antecedaneam, sed ut medium illis destinatum et conferendum quos Deus elegit, et adoptandos destinavit.
english: On the Minor, which sits in express Scripture words, little need be added: from what is said it is plain you cannot prove from it that faith in election must be taken as a foreseen condition antecedent to election — but as a means destined and to be given to those God elected and destined for adoption.

source_text: Arg. 6. Petitur aliud argumentum a perpetuo usu vocis, Electi, quotiescunque ponitur cum respectu ad salutem; ut Rom. viii. Quis accusabit adversus electos Dei? et Rom. xi. Electi assecuti sunt, et Matth. xxii. Multi vocati, pauci electi. Ex hisce aliisque locis consimilibus ita argumentantur; Vox Electorum, cum de salute agitur, perpetuo in Scripturis usurpatur pro credentibus: Ergo nulla est electio ad salutem nisi credentium.
english: Arg. 6. Another argument from the standing use of Elect wherever salvation is in view — Rom. 8: Who will accuse God's elect?; Rom. 11: The elect have obtained; Matt. 22: Many called, few elect. From these and like places: the word Elect, when Scripture speaks of salvation, is always used for believers; therefore there is no election to salvation except of believers.

source_text: Sol. Quando sacrae Scripturae loquuntur de aliquibus designatis personis tanquam de Electis, hoc vocabulum accommodant ad solos credentes: quia nos de arcano Electionis nihil certi habemus nisi a posteriore, hoc est, ab effectis fidei et sanctificationis. Hinc Apostolus credentes Electorum nomine passim solet notare. Verum inde non efficitur, vel debere confundi electos et credentes, vel electionem ex praevisa fide tanquam conditione antecedanea esse suspendendam. Quamvis enim nos non possumus eos electos vocare, quos videmus incredulos, tamen certum est, multos impoenitentes ac incredulos esse tamen interim electos: quod in Paulo, adeoque in omnibus electis, ante efficacem conversionem, verissimum est. Quin etiam cum Praedestinationis et Electionis vocabula in tota hac disputatione promiscue usurpentur, planum est vocem Praedestinatorum, cum de salute agitur, etiam de incredulis usurpari. Nam cum Apostolus Rom. viii. 28. dicit, Quos Praedestinavit, Vocavit; quos vocavit justificavit, &c. aperte ponit Praedestinatos quosdam antecedenter ad vocationem, fidem et justificationem.
english: Sol. When Scripture names designated persons Elect, it fits the word to believers alone — because we know nothing sure of election's secret except a posteriori, from the effects of faith and sanctification. So the Apostle often marks believers as Elect. That does not mean elect and believers must be confused, or that election hangs on foresight of faith as an antecedent condition. We cannot call unbelievers elect as we see them — yet many impenitent and unbelieving are elect in the meantime; true of Paul and of all the elect before efficacious conversion. And since Predestination and Election are used interchangeably in this dispute, Predestinated in salvation-talk is used even of unbelievers. Rom. 8:28ff.: Whom he predestinated, he called; whom he called, he justified — openly sets some Predestinated before vocation, faith, and justification.

source_text: Hisce accedat, In illis omnibus locis ubi Electorum nomen tribuitur fidelibus, fidem actualem semper denotari, non illam ante jacta mundi fundamenta in sola Dei praescientia consideratam, quam urgent Remonstrantes. Non recte igitur inferunt; Electus et credens sunt subjecta eadem secundum phrasin Scripturarum: Ergo Electio fit ex praevisa fide; sed, Ergo omnibus electis suo tempore datur fides salutifera. Possem facile hoc argumentum invertere, et contra adversarios sic retorquere, si quid roboris in se haberet, Vox Credentium, cum de credentibus ad salutem agitur, perpetuo intelligitur de electis: Ergo nulla est fides ad salutem nisi electorum; Ergo fides oritur ex antecedente electione. Sed ex tali usu vocabulorum nihil aliud concludi debet, quam fidem et electionem habere inter se quendam nexum: sed utrum ita connectantur ut fides praevisa antecedat electionem tanquam conditio in eligendo praerequisita, (quod volunt Remonstrantes) an ut fides subsequatur electionem tanquam dispositio in omnibus electis debito tempore producenda, ex locis Scripturae allatis non constat. Ea igitur sigillatim expendere minime necessarium est.
english: Add: wherever Elect is given to the faithful, actual faith is meant — not faith merely in God's foresight before the world's foundations, which the Remonstrants urge. So they wrongly infer: Elect and believer are the same subjects in Scripture's phrasing, therefore election is from foresight of faith. Rather: therefore to all the elect in their time saving faith is given. If the argument had force I could invert it: Believers, when salvation is in view, always means the elect; therefore no saving faith except of the elect; therefore faith arises from antecedent election. From such word-use you may conclude only that faith and election have a nexus — not whether foresight of faith precedes election as a prerequired condition (as Remonstrants will), or faith follows election as a disposition to be produced in all the elect at the due time. The cited places do not settle that; weighing them one by one is needless.

source_text: Arg. 7. Τρόπος secundum quem Dominus Deus in aliis ostendit suam misericordiam, in aliis justitiam, est vera et unica praedestinatio; Atqui decretum salvandi credentes ex una, condemnandi incredulos ex altera parte, est talis τρόπος: Ergo hoc decretum est vera et unica praedestinatio. Dicunt Majorem ab ipsis Contraremonstrantibus admitti: Minorem probari ex Rom. ix. 22. ubi per vasa misericordiae et irae intelliguntur credentes et increduli.
english: Arg. 7. The τρόπος by which the Lord shows his mercy in some and his justice in others is the true and only predestination. But the decree to save believers on one side and condemn unbelievers on the other is such a τρόπος. Therefore that decree is the true and only predestination. They say Contraremonstrants admit the Major; the Minor they prove from Rom. 9:22, where vessels of mercy and of wrath mean believers and unbelievers.

source_text: Sol. In mente Divina concipere oportet quoad Electos praeordinationem duplicem: unam, quae ordinem intentionis continet; alteram, quae ordinem exsecutionis: Utraque autem inservit declarandae misericordiae et justitiae Divinae. Exempli causa; Quod Deus ante jacta mundi fundamenta decreverit Jacobum et Petrum diligere, ac eorundem in donatione gratiae specialis ac vitae aeternae misereri; Esavum autem et Judam in hac designatione ad infallibilem vitae gratiaeque consecutionem praeterire, atque in peccatis suis obfirmatos justae condemnationi deputare: in hisce, inquam, decretis continetur abyssus quaedam misericordiae et justitiae, cujus penetrandae nulla acies humani ingenii sufficit. Jam vero quod idem Deus in verbo suo patefecerit, se decrevisse omnes credentes salvare, omnes incredulos damnare, quodque (in die judicii) cum ad exsecutionem ventum fuerit, de facto Esavum et Judam damnet, Jacobum et Petrum servet: exprimit etiam misericordiae justitiaeque Divinae egregium ac singulare specimen.
english: Sol. In God's mind regarding the elect, conceive a double praeordination: one of intention, one of execution — both serve to declare divine mercy and justice. Example: before the world's foundations God decreed to love Jacob and Peter and have mercy on them in special grace and eternal life; to pass by Esau and Judas for that infallible attainment of life and grace, and appoint those hardened in their sins to just condemnation — an abyss of mercy and justice no human wit can pierce. And that the same God has opened in his word that he decreed to save all believers and damn all unbelievers, and that on judgment day he in fact damns Esau and Judas and saves Jacob and Peter — that too is a singular specimen of divine mercy and justice.

source_text: Cum igitur in utraque praeordinatione elucescat misericordia ac justitia Divina; hoc est, tam in ea qua Deus decrevit singulares quasdam personas facere credentes, quam in ea altera qua eisdem credentibus vitam aeternam promittit et praestat; tam in ea qua decrevit quarundam personarum non misereri eousque ut easdem emolliat, fidemque illis inspiret; quam in ea qua eosdem obduratos et incredulos damnat: non debuerunt adversarii ad posteriorem τρόπον alligare totam et integram praedestinationis rationem; quae propriissime versatur in priori. Hisce praelibatis, dico Majorem syllogismi propositi non esse universalem. Nam omnis τρόπος in quo apparet erga alios misericordia, erga alios justitia Dei, non est illa unica praedestinatio cujus inscrutabilem profunditatem Scripturae tantopere celebrant; quamvis in ipsa praedestinatione proprie sumpta, qua alii ad vitam mediante gratia speciali destinantur, alii in morte mediante proprio demerito relinquuntur, misericordia ac justitia illustrissime agant partes suas.
english: So in both praeordinations mercy and justice shine — in the decree to make certain persons believers, and in the decree that promises and gives those believers eternal life; in the decree not to have mercy so far as to soften some and inspire faith, and in the decree that damns the same hardened unbelievers. Adversaries should not bind the whole reason of predestination to the latter τρόπος; it turns most properly on the former. With that premised: the Major is not universal. Not every τρόπος in which mercy toward some and justice toward others appears is that unique predestination whose depth Scripture so celebrates — though in predestination properly taken, by which some are destined to life by special grace and others left in death by their own demerit, mercy and justice play their parts most clearly.

source_text: Accedo ad Minorem, in qua affirmatur, decretum salvandi credentes, et condemnandi incredulos, esse illam praeordinationem secundum quam Deus erga alios declarat misericordiam suam, erga alios justitiam suam. Fatemur juxta hoc decretum spectari et declarari in eventu misericordiam Dei erga alios, et erga alios justitiam: verum longe altiori modo exserit se misericordia in praedestinationis decreto, et justitia in decreto praeteritionis. Decretum hoc, Ego salvabo credentes, Ego condemnabo incredulos, in se consideratum omnibus ex aequo ostendit et facit misericordiam, omnibus ex aequo ostendit et facit justitiam: Nihil promittit aut exhibet Jacobo et Petro, quod non sub iisdem conditionibus promittit et exhibet Esavo et Judae; nihil negat Esavo aut Judae quod non sub iisdem conditionibus negat Jacobo et Petro. Nam quod Jacobus et Petrus participes fiant misericordiae et vitae aeternae, Esavus et Judas non fiant, id discriminis non fluxit ex decretorum diversitate quoad ipsas personas, sed ex personarum diversitate in suis operationibus.
english: Now the Minor: that the decree to save believers and condemn unbelievers is the praeordination by which God declares mercy toward some and justice toward others. We grant that on that decree mercy and justice are seen and declared in the event — but mercy puts itself forth far higher in the predestination decree, and justice in the decree of passing by. I will save believers, I will condemn unbelievers, taken in itself, shows and makes mercy equally to all, justice equally to all. It promises Jacob and Peter nothing it does not under the same conditions promise Esau and Judas; it denies Esau or Judas nothing it does not under the same conditions deny Jacob and Peter. That Jacob and Peter share mercy and eternal life while Esau and Judas do not comes not from diverse decrees about the persons, but from the persons' diversity in their operations.

source_text: Illa autem misericordia quae in decreto praedestinationis se exserit, decernit, praeparat, donat singulari alicui praedestinatae personae quod alii non praedestinatae minime decernit, praeparat aut donat. Illa etiam Justitia quae in decreto reprobationis consideratur, decernit aliquid negandum reprobato quod idem decernitur haud negandum Praedestinato. Non igitur sufficit ad constituendum praedestinationis proprie dictae decretum, quod secundum illud intervenientibus diversis humani arbitrii actibus, misericordia in hos, justitia in illos exseratur; sed requiritur tale decretum quod ex primaria intentione et speciali operatione Dei decernentis, includat misericordiam hisce exhibendam; et ex liberrima et justissima Dei voluntate innuat eandem specialem misericordiam aliis denegandam.
english: But the mercy that puts itself forth in the predestination decree decrees, prepares, and gifts to a singular predestinated person what it does not decree, prepare, or gift to one not predestinated. The justice in the reprobation decree decrees something denied to the reprobate that is not denied to the Predestinated. So it is not enough for predestination properly so called that, with diverse acts of human choice intervening, mercy falls on these and justice on those. What is required is a decree that, from God's primary intention and special operation in decreeing, includes mercy to be shown to these, and from his freest, most just will hints that the same special mercy is to be denied to others.

source_text: Arg. 8. Ab ordine exsecutionis sic disputant; Illi et tales quos et quales Deus in tempore salvat et perdit, illos et tales ab aeterno decrevit salvare et perdere: Atqui Deus solos perseverantes in fide, qua tales, in tempore salvat; incredulos, qua tales, perdit: Ergo Deus ab aeterno decrevit solos fideles, qua tales, salvare. Majorem probant ab immutabilitate Dei: Minorem ex perpetua voce Evangelii, quod credentibus vitam pollicetur, incredulis mortem interminatur.
english: Arg. 8. From the order of execution they argue: those and such as God saves and destroys in time, he decreed from eternity to save and destroy. But in time God saves only those who persevere in faith, as such, and destroys unbelievers as such. Therefore from eternity he decreed to save only the faithful as such. They prove the Major from God's immutability; the Minor from the Gospel's standing voice — life promised to believers, death threatened to unbelievers.

source_text: Sol. Conclusionem dicimus non directe contradicere sententiae nostrae. Conclusum enim oportuit, Ergo Deus solos fideles, et qua fideles, ex praevisione hujus fidei elegit ad gloriam. Illa autem conclusio, Ergo solos fideles ab aeterno decrevit, qua tales servare, ponit fidem antecedaneam conditionem quoad ipsam externam collationem decretae salutis; quod nos non negamus; non autem quoad ipsum internum decretum Dei ad salutem destinantis; quod probatum oportuit. Ad Majoris ventilationem accedamus. Dico in illa commisceri, et mala fide copulari duo vocabula, quorum unum designat ipsam destinationem ad salutem in mente Divina; alterum perductionem ad salutem in exsecutione externa. Nam verbum Decernere respicit actum voluntatis Divinae aeternum et intrinsecum; verbum Servare respicit effectum extrinsecum et temporalem.
english: Sol. The conclusion does not directly contradict us. What they needed was: therefore God elected to glory only the faithful as faithful, from foresight of that faith. Their conclusion — he decreed from eternity to save only the faithful as such — makes faith an antecedent condition for the external conferring of decreed salvation (which we grant), not for God's internal destinating decree (which they needed to prove). On the Major: two words are mixed in bad faith — one names destination to salvation in the divine mind, the other leading to salvation in external execution. Decernere looks to the eternal intrinsic act of will; Servare to the extrinsic temporal effect.

source_text: Jam vero actus Dei internus non habet eas causas, nec requirit eas conditiones praecedaneas, quas habet et praerequirit ipsum externum salutis praedictae effectum. Non servat Petrum Deus nisi fide ejus praecedente; at decernit servare Petrum in gratuito et aeterno voluntatis suae beneplacito, non praecedente hac fide tanquam conditione ad decreti ipsius constitutionem, sed tanquam conditione ad rei decretae opportunam temporalemque effectionem. Caput ergo erroris est, quod qualitas fidei antecedanea, quae cum re decreta conjungi debuit, et eidem in sola exsecutione praeponi, cum actu Dei decernentis conjungatur, et decreto ejus tanquam antecedaneum motivum praeponatur.
english: God's internal act does not have the causes or require the antecedent conditions that the external effect of salvation has and prerequires. He does not save Peter unless Peter's faith precedes; yet he decrees to save Peter in the free eternal good pleasure of his will — not with that faith as a condition for constituting the decree, but as a condition for timely temporal effecting of what was decreed. The error's head: the antecedent quality of faith, which should be joined to the thing decreed and set before it only in execution, is joined to God's decreeing act and set before the decree as an antecedent motive.

source_text: Exemplo illustrabimus ea quae dicta sunt, et ostendemus quasdam conditiones requiri posse ut previas, quo Petrus servetur, vel in regnum caeleste introducatur, quae non requiruntur ut previae, quo eligatur, sive ad vitam aeternam a Deo destinetur. Ponamus Regem aliquem, conspecto mendico pannis obsito, ulceribus foetido, decernere nihilominus ex mero suo beneplacito hunc talem adoptare, et ad regni coronam evehere; insuper tamen ordinare ut antequam coronetur, regalibus vestimentis induatur, et ab immunditie sua purgetur, neque coronetur nisi prius ita fuerit purgatus et indutus. Quis non videt pulchra haec vestimenta et purgationem decreta et praerequisita fuisse tanquam praecedanea ad actum coronandi, et tamen non fuisse praerequisita tanquam praecedanea motiva ad primam destinationem regni et coronae?
english: An example: some conditions can be required beforehand so that Peter is saved or brought into the heavenly kingdom, without being required beforehand so that he is elected or destined by God to eternal life. Suppose a king sees a beggar in rags, foul with ulcers, yet from mere good pleasure decrees to adopt him and raise him to the kingdom's crown — and also orders that before crowning he be clothed in royal garments and purged of uncleanness, and not crowned until thus purged and clothed. Who does not see those fair garments and the purging were decreed and prerequired as antecedent to crowning, yet not as antecedent motives for the first destination of kingdom and crown?

source_text: Fiat ergo syllogismus ad exemplar propositum a Remonstrantibus, et vanitas ejus illico patebit: Ille et talis quem et qualem hic Rex in tempore coronavit, illum et talem ab initio coronare decrevit: Sed pulchre vestitum et a squalore suo purgatum, qua talem, in tempore coronat: Ergo ab initio decrevit pulchre vestitum, qua talem, hoc est, ex praevisa conditione pulchrorum vestimentorum, adoptare et coronare. Nugae merae. Non enim prima voluntas adoptandi et coronandi originem cepit ab antecedanea consideratione, aut praevisa conditione pulchrorum vestimentorum; sed ipsa actio coronandi requirebat haec vestimenta et hanc purgationem antecedaneam, idque ex decreto Regis externam rei exsecutionem ordinante. Accommodemus haec praesenti instituto. Deus Petrum, Paulum, vel quemlibet electum in massa veteris Adami corruptum et peccato tabidum, ex beneplacito mero voluntatis suae vult adoptare, et aeterna vita donare: Sed decernit etiam, et in Evangelio hoc decretum promulgat, velle se ut fide prius purificetur, et a sordibus peccatorum mundetur, quam in possessionem regni introducatur.
english: Run the Remonstrants' pattern and its vanity shows at once: whom and as such this king crowned in time, he decreed from the start to crown as such; but in time he crowns one beautifully clothed and purged of squalor as such; therefore from the start he decreed to adopt and crown one beautifully clothed as such — i.e. from foresight of fair garments. Mere trifles. The first will to adopt and crown did not spring from foresight of garments; crowning itself required those garments and that prior purging, by the king's decree ordering external execution. Apply it: God from mere good pleasure wills to adopt Peter, Paul, or any elect corrupt in old Adam's mass and wasting in sin, and gift eternal life — yet also decrees, and publishes in the Gospel, that he wills him first purified by faith and cleansed from sin's filth before entering the kingdom.

source_text: Erit jam consideratio Petri ut fidelis et a peccatis purgati antecedanea ad exsecutionem rei volitae; salutis scilicet acquisitionem, idque ex decreto Dei: sed non erit antecedanea ad ipsam voluntatem Dei de Petro servando, qui utrumque decrevit, et servare Petrum, et priusquam servetur fide illum donare. Neque immutabilitatem Divinae naturae labefactat quod ponitur, decernere aliquid tanquam praecedaneum ad rei decretae actualem productionem, quod non est praecedaneum ad internam Dei de re producenda volitionem. Ratio manifesta est; Quia Effectum salutis in subjecto praedestinato et decretum salutis dandae in voluntate praedestinantis sunt res diversae, nec easdem causas aut conditiones previas requirunt. De Minore nil aliud dico, quam multa praerequiri ut quis in tempore salvatur, quae non erant praerequisita ut ab aeterno ad salutem eligeretur, sed potius media praedestinato postmodum conferenda ut ad salutem perduceretur.
english: Peter as faithful and purged of sins is antecedent to executing what was willed — acquiring salvation, by God's decree — but not antecedent to God's will to save Peter, who decreed both: to save Peter, and to gift him faith before he is saved. Nor does that unsettle divine immutability: something may be decreed as antecedent to actually producing what was decreed without being antecedent to God's internal volition about producing it. Reason: the effect of salvation in the predestinated subject and the decree to give salvation in the predestinating will are diverse things and do not require the same prior causes or conditions. On the Minor: many things are prerequired for someone to be saved in time that were not prerequired for eternal election to salvation — rather means later conferred on the predestinated so he is led through to salvation.

source_text: Arg. 9. Illud Dei de salute humana decretum cujus fundamentum est Christus, est ipsissima electio ad salutem: Decretum Dei de salvandis credentibus est illud decretum salutis cujus fundamentum est Christus: Ergo decretum de salvandis fidelibus est ipsissima electio ad salutem. Majorem dicunt esse manifestam; quia nulla est salus vel benedictio ad salutem nisi in Christo. Minorem aeque perspicuam asserunt; quandoquidem illud unicum decretum est fundamentum Christianismi, salutis, et certitudinis de salute: Christianismi; quia eo constituitur Christus a Deo Salvator et Caput eorum qui participes salutis futuri sunt: Salutis; quia hoc est decretum εὐδοκίας sive beneplaciti Dei in Christo, cui tota salus nostra innititur: Certitudinis de salute; quandoquidem certitudo nostra omnis huic fulcro innixa est; Credentes salvabuntur: Ego credo: Ergo Ego salvabor.
english: Arg. 9. God's decree on human salvation whose foundation is Christ is election itself to salvation. The decree to save believers is that salvation-decree founded on Christ. Therefore the decree to save the faithful is election itself. They call the Major plain — no salvation or blessing unto salvation except in Christ. The Minor equally clear: that one decree is the foundation of Christianity, of salvation, and of certainty of salvation — Christianity, because by it God constitutes Christ Savior and Head of those who will share salvation; salvation, because it is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ on which our whole salvation rests; certainty, because all our assurance rests on this prop: Believers will be saved; I believe; therefore I will be saved.

source_text: Sol. Observandum est, in nullo argumento Remonstrantium debitam conclusionem prodire. Nam aliud est concludere, Ergo decretum de salvandis credentibus est ipsissima electio ad salutem; aliud, Ergo Electio ipsissima ad salutem fit ex praevisione fidei antecedaneae. Hanc conclusionem frustra exspectavimus, quae nusquam visa est comparere. Sed rationem praedictam, qualem qualem, discutiamus. Major imperfecte admodum explicat rationem Electionis; nec vera est usquequaque, si universaliter intelligatur, sicuti oportet, nisi syllogismum vaders velimus nobis obtrudere. Fiat ergo universalis, hoc modo, Omne Dei de salute humana decretum cujus fundamentum est Christus, est ipsissima singularium personarum electio ad salutem. Attexatur Minor, At decretum de salvandis credentibus (id est, quibuslibet hominibus, si credant) est illud decretum salutis cujus fundamentum est Christus: Ergo hoc decretum de salvandis Credentibus est ipsissima singularium personarum electio ad salutem.
english: Sol. Notice: in no Remonstrant argument does the owed conclusion appear. One thing is to conclude that the decree to save believers is election itself; another, that election itself is from foresight of antecedent faith — the conclusion we waited for in vain and never saw. Discuss their reason as it stands. The Major explains election quite imperfectly, and is not true throughout if taken universally as it must be, unless we let a slippery syllogism be forced on us. Make it universal: every divine decree on human salvation whose foundation is Christ is election itself of singular persons to salvation. Attach the Minor: the decree to save believers (any men, if they believe) is that Christ-founded salvation decree. Therefore that decree is election itself of singular persons.

source_text: Ut detegantur errores hujus argumentationis, sciendum, diversa decreta de salute humana in considerationem nostram venire posse, quorum omnium fundamentum est Christus, et tamen in illis omnibus ipsissima Electio non consistit. Sunt primo decreta nota et omnibus promulgata, quae exprimunt et continent, quibus conditionibus, vel quibus modis et mediis homines sunt ad salutem perducendi — qualia sunt, Ego salvabo omnes qui resipiscent, qui credent in Messiam, qui in hac fide et vitae novitate ad extremum usque perseverabunt. Talibus decretis omnes mortales promiscue edocentur, quibus conditionibus impletis liceat illis salutem exspectare. At iisdem nullae singulares personae ad salutem prae aliis a Deo ponuntur electae aut praedestinatae. Illorum decretorum Christus est fundamentum: quia Deus nunquam dignatus fuisset cum homine corrupto et rebelli sub talibus conditionibus agere, aut vitam aeternam credenti et resipiscenti promittere, nisi interveniente hoc novi foederis Mediatore in quo omnes promissiones Dei sunt Etiam et Amen. In hisce tamen decretis ratio electionis non includitur: quia positis talibus decretis, quae vitam omnibus peccatoribus promiscue offerunt, si crediderint et resipuerint, nisi etiam accederet aliud purae misericordiae decretum, nemo servaretur, quia nemo crederet.
english: To expose the errors: diverse decrees on human salvation can come into view, all founded on Christ, yet election itself does not consist in all of them. First are known decrees published to all, stating under what conditions or by what means men are led to salvation — I will save all who repent, believe in the Messiah, and persevere in that faith and newness of life to the end. By those, all mortals are taught what conditions let them expect salvation. But they set no singular persons elected or predestinated before others. Christ is their foundation: God would never have deigned to deal with corrupt rebellious man under such terms, or promise eternal life to the believing and repenting, without this new-covenant Mediator in whom all God's promises are Yea and Amen. Yet election's reason is not in them: with life offered promiscuously to all sinners if they believe and repent, unless another decree of pure mercy also came, no one would be saved, because no one would believe.

source_text: Secundo, est aliud genus decretorum quo in mente et voluntate Divina ab aeterno designantur singulares personae ad salutem infallibiliter perducendae. Non nominantur quidem ipsa individua in libro Scripturae; sed inscribuntur tamen ipsa individua in libro vitae, Phil. iv. 3. Luc. x. 20. De hisce intelliguntur illa Scripturarum loca, Deus novit suos, 2 Tim. ii. 19. Ille vocat oves suas nominatim, Joan. x. 3. Ego novi quos elegerim, Joan. xiii. 18. Tertio, est cum praedicto de personis decreto colligatum semper et connexum decretum donandi singularibus illis personis omnia gratiae efficacis media, per quae ad salutem perducantur. Huc spectat illud Apostoli, Rom. viii. 30. Quos praedestinavit, vocavit; et quos vocavit, justificavit, &c. Et Ephes. i. 3–4. Benedixit nobis Deus omni benedictione spirituali, sicut elegit nos antequam jacerentur mundi fundamenta. Electio ante tempora saecularia est quasi mensura omnium spiritualium benedictionum (puta fidei, sanctitatis, perseverantiae) quae dantur in tempore; non vice versa (ut volunt Remonstrantes) praevisa fides et perseverantia, mensura electionis. Haec etiam decreta, juxta quae personae singulares ad vitam praedestinantur, et iisdem gratia salutifera praeparatur, habent Christum pro fundamento. In eo enim eliguntur tanquam membra Christo Capiti suo tempore unienda; ac per et propter eum gratia speciali hae singulares personae imbuuntur. Major itaque propositio duobus nominibus falsa est et rejicienda. Primo, quod supponit Christum solummodo fundamentum esse decreti illius universalis, Omnes credentes salvabo; cum etiam fundamentum sit hujus singularis decreti, Ego Petro, Paulo, et sic de singulis electis, vitam aeternam dabo: Ego illis singulis fidem, perseverantiam, uno verbo, gratiam ad salutem efficaciter perducentem, dabo. Secundo, falsa est Major, quod electionem in illo universali decreto formaliter constitutam supponit, cum ea se exserat in secundo decreto quo personae singulares ad vitam eliguntur, et in tertio, quo ad media efficacia prae aliis participanda destinantur, juxta celebrem apud Theologos praedestinationis definitionem, praedestinatio est praeparatio gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro.
english: Second: another kind of decrees by which from eternity singular persons are designated in God's mind and will to be led infallibly to salvation. The individuals are not named in Scripture's book, yet they are written in the book of life (Phil. 4:3; Luke 10:20). Of these: God knows his own (2 Tim. 2:19); he calls his sheep by name (John 10:3); I know whom I have chosen (John 13:18). Third: always bound to that person-decree is a decree to gift those singular persons every means of efficacious grace by which they are led to salvation. So Rom. 8:30 — whom he predestinated he called, whom he called he justified — and Eph. 1:3–4. Election before the ages is as it were the measure of all spiritual blessings given in time (faith, holiness, perseverance); not the reverse, as Remonstrants will, foresight faith and perseverance measuring election. These decrees too have Christ for foundation: in him they are elected as members to be united in time to Christ their Head, and through and for him they are imbued with special grace. So the Major is false twice: it makes Christ foundation only of I will save all believers, when he is also foundation of I will give eternal life to Peter, Paul, and each elect — faith, perseverance, grace leading effectively to salvation. And it locates election formally in that universal decree, whereas election puts itself forth in the second decree electing singular persons to life and the third destinating them to efficacious means before others — per the theologians' definition: predestination is preparation of grace now and glory hereafter.

source_text: Ad Minorem verbo respondere sufficit; Christum esse fundamentum generalis ejus decreti de salvandis quibuscunque sub conditione fidei; sed non ejus solius, verum etiam aliorum decretorum, secundum quae singularibus personis, Christo a Patre datis ante jacta mundi fundamenta, gratia et gloria suo tempore donabitur. Non debuerunt Remonstrantes tam obstinato silentio obruere haec posteriora decreta, et in illo primo universali haerere, nisi opinentur nullum unquam fuisse decretum in mente Divina de singularibus personis efficaci gratia imbuendis, et per talem gratiam ad gloriam perducendis. Pergamus, et ea pensitemus quae ad confirmationem utriusque propositionis adducta sunt. Majorem clamant esse manifestam, quia nulla est salus vel benedictio ad salutem nisi in Christo. Frivola probatio. An quia nullum beneficium decernitur in nos conferendum nisi in Christo, idcirco quodlibet decretum ad salutem nostram spectans, cujus fundamentum est Christus, erit ipsissima nostra electio? Tam hoc cohaeret quam arena sine calce. Sed Minorem perspicuam etiam esse dicunt, quia illud unicum decretum, Ego salvabo omnes Credentes, est fundamentum Christianismi, salutis, et certitudinis de salute. Respondeo, illud unicum decretum generale non esse fundamentum Christianismi. Sunt enim alia Christianismi fundamenta, et inter alia illud praecipuum fundamentum; Fidem et perseverantiam, ac quicquid ad caelum ducit infallibiliter, esse specialia specialis gratiae dona, non autem contingentia effecta ex arbitrio hominis nondum electi nascentia, et electionis Divinae motiva.
english: On the Minor in a word: Christ is foundation of that general decree to save whosoever under the condition of faith — but not of that alone; also of other decrees by which singular persons, given by the Father to Christ before the world's foundations, will in their time be gifted grace and glory. Remonstrants should not bury those later decrees in obstinate silence and stick in the first universal one, unless they think there never was a decree in God's mind to imbue singular persons with efficacious grace and lead them by it to glory. They cry the Major plain because no salvation except in Christ — a frivolous proof. Because no benefit is decreed for us except in Christ, is every Christ-founded salvation-decree therefore our election itself? That coheres like sand without lime. They say the Minor is clear because I will save all Believers founds Christianity, salvation, and certainty. I answer: that general decree alone is not Christianity's foundation. There are others — chief among them that faith, perseverance, and whatever leads infallibly to heaven are special gifts of special grace, not contingent effects from the choice of a man not yet elected, and motives of divine election.

source_text: Porro, hoc fundamentum quod nos asserimus, multo magis probat Christum a Deo constitutum Salvatorem et Caput eorum qui servabuntur, quam illud generale quod ab istis urgetur. Nam in illo, Omnes qui credent salvabuntur, pactum salutis cum humano genere initum ostenditur propter Christum; sed quod effectu carebit nisi conditio credendi a nobis impleatur; qua de re in illo decreto nihil constitutum est. At quando defendimus, Deum insuper decrevisse propter Christum dare gratiam fidem et vitam omnibus electis, et ex plenitudine ejus realiter in eos diffundere hanc gratiam efficacem et salutiferam: non nudo pacto, sed ipso facto facimus Christum Salvatorem, et Caput eorum omnium qui fiunt salutis participes. Adhaec illud generale decretum, Omnes credentes salvabuntur, non est decretum illud εὐδοκίας cui tota salus nostra innititur. Nam hoc decretum est, ut sic dicam, declarativum et doctrinale; sed salus singularium personarum niti debet decreto Dei practico et operante. Misere ageretur nobiscum, si tota nostra salus niteretur hoc pacto conditionato, Si credideris salvus eris, et non esset aliud εὐδοκίας Divinae decretum de fide nobis danda, nobisque efficaciter servandis. Denique illud generale decretum, Omnes credentes salvabuntur, non potest esse alicui personae singulari fundamentum sufficiens certitudinis de salute sua. Nam illud decretum neminem servat sua sola virtute: Imo multi damnabuntur qui sciunt et credunt omnes credentes et resipiscentes fore salvandos. Accedat ergo oportet ad certitudinem faciendam alterius decreti efficacia; Nimirum, quod ego credam, quod ego in finem usque perseverabо. At unde haec certitudo fidei meae, et perseverantiae meae? Non a contingente meo libero arbitrio; ergo ab immutabili aliquo decreto Divino. Si igitur rem spectemus, certitudo salutis quoad hanc vel illam personam singularem niti debet decreto aliquo Dei practico infallibiliter decernente et operante salutem ejusdem. Si certam rei cognitionem quoad nos: certitudo salutis nostrae niti debet revelatione aliqua ejusdem decreti, per Spiritum adoptionis, et effecta ejusdem in cordibus singulorum. Nam Spiritus ille testificatur spiritui nostro nos esse illos Dei filios, quos destinavit aeternae vitae, quosque sanctificavit in hoc saeculo, ut possit glorificare in futuro. Caeterum in illo universali decreto per modum legis promulgato, Quisquis crediderit salvus erit, nec certa salus cujusquam singularis personae fundari potest, nec certa cognitio cujusquam de salute sua infallibiliter futura. Atque haec sunt omnia illa argumenta, quibus Collocutores conati sunt stabilire electionem hominum singularium ex antecedanea fidei praevisae conditione. Quae omnia ex Arminii scriptis desumpta sunt.
english: Further: the foundation we assert proves far more that God constituted Christ Savior and Head of those who will be saved than their general one. All who will believe will be saved shows a pact of salvation with the human race for Christ's sake — but it lacks effect unless we fulfill the believing condition, about which that decree constitutes nothing. When we defend that God further decreed for Christ's sake to give grace, faith, and life to all the elect, and from his fullness really pour efficacious saving grace into them, we make Christ Savior and Head of all who share salvation not by bare pact but by the fact itself. Besides, All believers will be saved is not the good-pleasure decree our whole salvation rests on — it is, so to speak, declarative and doctrinal; singular persons' salvation must rest on a practical operating decree of God. It would go miserably with us if all our salvation rested on If you believe you will be saved, with no further good-pleasure decree to give us faith and save us efficaciously. Finally that general decree cannot be any singular person's sufficient certainty of his salvation: it saves no one by its own virtue alone — many will be damned who know and believe all believers and repenting will be saved. Certainty needs another decree's efficacy: that I believe, that I will persevere to the end. Whence that certainty of my faith and perseverance? Not from my contingent free choice — therefore from some immutable divine decree. As to the thing: certainty for this or that singular person rests on a practical decree infallibly decreeing and working that person's salvation. As to our knowledge: certainty rests on some revelation of that decree through the Spirit of adoption and its effects in individuals' hearts — that Spirit witnesses to our spirit that we are those sons of God destined to eternal life, sanctified in this age to be glorified hereafter. In the universal law-form decree Whoever believes will be saved, neither certain salvation of any singular person nor certain knowledge of one's infallibly future salvation can be founded. And these are all the Collocutors' arguments trying to establish election of singular men from the antecedent condition of foresight faith — all taken from Arminius's writings.

source_text: Cap. V. Objectiones quaedam Arminianae a Collocutoribus omissae ponuntur et dissolvuntur. Alia apud Arminium occurrunt nonnulla alia argumenta, quae in Collatione Hagiensi non adhibentur; nos ea quoque in medium afferemus, et sigillatim pertractabimus. Ejus generis quamplurima afferuntur in Examine Praedestinationis Perkinsianae; nonnulla alibi: quae uti sese nobis offerent discutiemus. Obj. 1. Electio est amor ad salutem: Deus non potest peccatorem amare ad salutem nisi ipsi sit reconciliatus: Non autem reconciliatur Deus nisi ei quem ut credentem in Christum intuetur: Ergo Deus neminem eligit nisi ex antecedaneo fidei intuitu.
english: Cap. V. Certain Arminian objections the Collocutors left out are set out and answered. Arminius has further arguments not used at the Hague Conference; we bring those in too and treat them one by one — many from his Examination of Perkinsian Predestination, some elsewhere. Obj. 1. Election is love unto salvation. God cannot love a sinner unto salvation unless reconciled to him. But God is reconciled only to one he looks on as believing in Christ. Therefore God elects no one except from an antecedent intuition of faith.

source_text: Sol. Electio est aeternum propositum sive decretum assumendi quosdam homines, aliis praeteritis, ad efficacem et infallibilem gratiae gloriaeque consecutionem: atque hoc sensu recte dicitur Amor ad salutem: Non amor in effectu externo adhuc effusus in electum, sed amor in proposito aeterno adhuc inclusus in ipso eligente. Sic Paulum nondum natum, nedum conversum aut credentem, Deus complectebatur suo arcano amore, habens scilicet in sese aeternum et immutabile propositum gratiam gloriamque eidem impertiendi. Transeat ergo illa prima propositio, Electionem esse amorem ad salutem.
english: Sol. Election is the eternal purpose or decree to take certain men, others passed by, to the efficacious infallible attainment of grace and glory — and in that sense it is rightly Love unto salvation: not love already poured out outwardly on the elect, but love still enclosed in the eternal purpose in the electing One himself. So God embraced Paul not yet born, much less converted or believing, with his secret love, having in himself an eternal immutable purpose to impart grace and glory to him. Let the first proposition pass: election is love unto salvation.

source_text: Quae attexuntur, scilicet, Deum non posse praedicto modo ad salutem amare quenquam nisi reconciliatum; reconciliari autem non posse cuiquam nisi ex antecedanea fidei ejus praevisione, sunt valde lubrica, imo manifeste falsa. Nam hoc amore, qui in electionis decreto latere intelligitur, Deus amat nondum reconciliatum eatenus ut illum sibi reconciliandum statuat; amat nondum fidelem, eatenus ut eum fide donandum decernat: quamvis non eo modo amet quo filios suos jam adoptatos, reconciliatos et credentes.
english: What they attach — that God cannot so love anyone unto salvation unless reconciled, and cannot be reconciled to anyone except from antecedent foresight of his faith — is very slippery, indeed plainly false. By the love latent in the election decree, God loves one not yet reconciled so far as to appoint him to be reconciled; loves one not yet faithful so far as to decree him gifted with faith — though not as he loves sons already adopted, reconciled, and believing.

source_text: Ipse Arminius, si sibi constare vellet, non posset inficias ire, Deum hoc amore electionis sive praedestinationis complecti electos et praedestinatos ante omnem fidei in illis praevisionem. Nam in Disputationibus publicis, Thes. 15, De praedestinatione, pag. 153, praedestinationem sic definit, Est decretum beneplaciti Dei in Christo quo apud se ab aeterno statuit fideles, quos fide donare decrevit, justificare, adoptare, vita aeterna donare, &c. Et in Examine Praedest. Perkins. concedit Deum non praescire homines crediturus priusquam praedestinaverit ut credant, pag. 32. Atque adjungit hanc rationem optimam sane et validissimam, Praescivit enim, inquit, eos suo dono crediturus, quod donum in praedestinatione praeparatum est, pag. 37. Atque huc etiam spectat quod alibi materiam praedestinationis duplicem ponit: Res divinas (quae benedictionum spiritualium nomine continentur) et personas quibus illarum communicatio est hoc decreto praedestinata. Quaero, Quomodo Deus eligit et praedestinat ex praevisa hominum fide, si in ipsa electione sive praedestinatione donum fidei sit hominibus decretum et praeparatum? Ridiculum est enim dicere, Deum in electione decernere et praeparare fidem certis hominibus, et tamen eosdem homines eligere ex antecedente intuitu fidei hanc ipsam electionem praecedentis; quasi Deus tum demum decerneret donum fidei huic aut illi singulari personae, quando antea perspexerit illum crediturum.
english: Arminius himself, if consistent, could not deny that by this election/predestination love God embraces the elect before all foresight of faith in them. In Public Disputations, Thesis 15 On predestination (p. 153), he defines: it is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ by which from eternity he determined to justify, adopt, and gift eternal life to the faithful whom he decreed to gift with faith. In the Examination of Perkinsian Predestination he grants God does not foreknow men as about to believe before he has predestinated them to believe (p. 32), and adds the strong reason: he foreknew they would believe by his gift, which gift is prepared in predestination (p. 37). Elsewhere he puts a double matter of predestination: divine things (spiritual blessings) and the persons to whom their communication is predestinated. I ask: how does God elect from foresight of faith if in election itself the gift of faith is decreed and prepared for men? It is ridiculous to say he decrees and prepares faith for certain men in election, yet elects them from an antecedent intuition of faith preceding that election — as if he only then decreed the gift of faith to this or that person when he had already seen he would believe.

source_text: Ut hoc incommodum vitaret Arminius, contendit non esse unum decretum quo statuit Deus, Volo fideli dare vitam, et, Volo huic dare fidem, sed distincta. Si sint distincta decreta, cur ipse Arminius in definitionem praedestinationis utrumque confecit? Porro, sint distincta (de quo nos minime laboramus) tamen cum sit praedestinatio sive electio certarum personarum ad fidem, necesse est ut haec electio praecedat omnem fidei intuitum in electis; necesse est ex amore oriatur hisce destinante quod aliis non decernitur. Denique, cum Deus ad fidem elegit singulares personas aliis praeteritis, manifestum est id eum non fecisse inscitum quod haec fides ad vitam aeternam infallibiliter obtinendam conducere; sed hoc potius donum Dei in hunc ipsum finem illis ordinasse et donasse. Exseruit igitur se amor ad salutem erga nondum credentes, praedestinando et praeparando illis donum fidei, quo mediante crederent, credentesque vitam aeternam adirent. Et sic videtis primam hanc objectionem Arminianam nullas vires habere.
english: To dodge the inconvenience Arminius claims there are not one but distinct decrees — I will give life to the faithful, and I will give faith to this one. If distinct, why did he himself put both in his definition of predestination? Let them be distinct (we care little): still, since there is predestination or election of certain persons to faith, that election must precede every intuition of faith in the elect; it must arise from love destinating to these what is not decreed to others. And when God elects singular persons to faith, others passed by, he does not do it unaware that this faith leads infallibly to eternal life — rather he ordained and gifted them that gift unto that end. So love unto salvation puts itself forth toward not-yet-believers by predestinating and preparing the gift of faith whereby they believe and, believing, enter eternal life. Thus this first Arminian objection has no force.

source_text: Obj. 2. Actualis vitae aeternae datio non magis est adstricta quam ejusdem dandae volitio: Sed ipsa datio adstricta est ad fideles, et fidem antecedentem praesupponit: Ergo et volitio dandae vitae aeternae, quae nihil aliud est quam electio. Electio itaque est ex fide praevisa. Arminius quique Arminium sectantur fere omnes ex hoc principio multa exstruunt argumenta, sed caduca et invalida.
english: Obj. 2. The actual gift of eternal life is no more bound than the will to give it. But the gift itself is bound to the faithful and presupposes antecedent faith. Therefore the will to give eternal life — which is nothing other than election — is likewise bound. So election is from foresight faith. Arminius and almost all who follow him build many arguments from this principle — frail and invalid.

source_text: Sol. Docet enim sana Philosophia, plura requiri tanquam instrumenta praecedanea ad productionem alicujus operis in actu externo, quam requiruntur tanquam antecedanea motiva ad intentionem sive destinationem ejusdem in mente et voluntate operantis. Fac enim me velle ita argumentari: Actualis domus alicujus aedificatio non magis est adstricta, quam ejusdem aedificandae volitio: Sed ipsa aedificatio adstricta est ad praecedaneam coaptationem lignorum et lapidum: Ergo ipsa volitio adstricta est ad haec omnia tanquam antecedanea, et ex illorum praevisione nascitur. Inepta sane conclusio.
english: Sol. Sound philosophy teaches that more is required as antecedent instruments to produce a work in an external act than as antecedent motives for intending or destinating that work in the operator's mind and will. Argue parallel: the actual building of a house is no more bound than the will to build it; but building is bound to the prior fitting of timbers and stones; therefore the will is bound to all those as antecedents and is born from foresight of them. An inept conclusion indeed.

source_text: Non enim ex praevisa coaptatione lapidum et lignorum nascebatur prima voluntas aedificandi in mente artificis; sed vice versa, ex voluntate aedificandi sequebatur illa prima lapidum et lignorum coagmentatio. Pari ratione, vita aeterna in effectu externo producta, et Petro aut Paulo collata, multa praesupponit quae vita aeterna ut in arcana Dei voluntate illis destinata non praerequirit. Destinare ad vitam, est actus immanens in mente Dei; dare vitam vel perducere ad vitam, est opus ad extra tendens in creaturam: illud perficitur et absolvitur solo actu voluntatis Divinae; hoc non perficitur nisi intervenientibus multis creaturae actionibus ex ordinatione Divina praerequisitis.
english: The craftsman's first will to build was not born from foresight of fitting stones and timbers — the reverse: from the will to build followed that first joining of stones and timbers. Likewise eternal life produced outwardly and conferred on Peter or Paul presupposes many things that eternal life as destinated to them in God's secret will does not prerequire. To destinate to life is an immanent act in God's mind; to give life or lead to life is a work tending outward on the creature. The former is finished by the sole act of the divine will; the latter is not finished without many creaturely actions intervening, prerequired by divine ordination.

source_text: Crassus igitur error est opinari, primam illam et aeternam personae alicujus singularis a Deo ad vitam destinationem iisdem legibus adstrictam, quibus temporalis consecutio quoad ipsos homines adstricta est. Idem enim Deus qui homini hanc legem dixit, Si credideris, dabo tibi vitam, vel salvus eris, nunquam hanc legem sibi imposuit, Si prius credideris, licebit mihi te praedestinare ad vitam; secus haud licebit.
english: So it is a crass error to think that God's first eternal destinating of a singular person to life is bound by the same laws that bind temporal attainment on the human side. The same God who told man, If you believe, I will give you life — or you will be saved — never bound himself: If you first believe, then I may predestinate you to life; otherwise I may not.

source_text: Obj. 3. Qualis existens accipit vitam aeternam, talis a Deo consideratus praedestinatus est ut acciperet: Sed solus fidelis accipit, et nemo alius: Ergo solus fidelis, idque ut consideratur fidelis, praedestinatus est ad accipiendam vitam aeternam.
english: Obj. 3. As one exists when receiving eternal life, so considered by God he was predestinated to receive it. But only the faithful receives, and no one else. Therefore only the faithful — and as considered faithful — was predestinated to receive eternal life.

source_text: Sol. Major multum in se habet ambiguitatis. Nam si eo sensu capiatur, quasi omnis ad vitam praedestinatus, antecedenter ad hoc decretum praedestinationis, talis existeret in intuitu Divino, qualis futurus est in ipsa acceptione vitae aeternae, prorsus rejicienda est.
