Si vero haec sit illius propositionis mens, Quando Deus electos ad vitam destinat, simul ab aeterno prospicit, et intuetur quales sit eos effecturus, antequam ad vitam perducat, eosdemque, ut tales, in vitae aeternae possessionem introducendos contempletur, id quidem verissimum est, nec negari potest, nisi quis negare velit Deum praescire quae ipse est facturus.
english: Sol. The Major is highly ambiguous. If it means every one predestinated to life already existed in God's intuition, before the predestination decree, as he will be in receiving eternal life — reject it outright. But if it means: when God destinates the elect to life, he at once from eternity looks ahead and sees of what sort he will make them before leading them to life, and contemplates them as such to be brought into possession of eternal life — that is most true, and cannot be denied unless one denies that God foreknows what he himself will do.

source_text: At hoc concesso non elicitur electio ex antecedanea fidei praevisione: sed certa in Deo fidei electorum praevisio infertur ex antecedanea electione, juxta illud celebre dictum, Actor. xiii. 48. Crediderunt quotquot ordinati fuerunt ad vitam aeternam. Unde etiam recte dicatur, Deum praevidere illos omnes crediturus, antequam accipiant vitam aeternam, quos decreto praedestinationis ad hanc vitam aeternam accipiendam ordinavit. Quod itaque Prosper de charitate dixit, id de fide etiam constanter affirmamus, Hoc tanto et tam ineffabili bono nemo inventus est dignus: Sed quicunque electus est a Deo, factus est dignus, de lib. arbit. pag. 125. Non dixit doctissimus Pater, et Pelagianorum ac Semipelagianorum Mastigium, Quicunque consideratus et praevisus ab ipso Deo ut dono charitatis aut fidei praeditus, ille postmodum ab eo electus est, sed, Quicunque a Deo electus est, ille postmodum fidei et charitatis factus est particeps.
english: Granted that, election is not drawn from antecedent foresight of faith — rather a sure foresight in God of the elects' faith is inferred from antecedent election, per Acts 13:48: as many as were ordained to eternal life believed. So God rightly foresees as about to believe, before they receive eternal life, all whom by the predestination decree he ordained to receive it. What Prosper said of charity we also affirm of faith (On Free Will, p. 125): of this so great, ineffable good no one was found worthy; but whoever was elected by God was made worthy. That learned Father, scourge of Pelagians and Semipelagians, did not say: whoever considered and foreseen as endowed with charity or faith was afterward elected — but: whoever was elected by God afterward became partaker of faith and charity.

source_text: Quicunque igitur vitam aeternam accepturus est, a Deo fuit praeconsideratus ut fidelis futurus, idque antecedenter ad acceptionem vitae aeternae: sed non fuit praevisus ut fidelis existens, idque antecedenter ad destinationem vitae aeternae. Hoc simili rem explicemus: Si quis in re bene lauta, conspecto misero et inope infante, statim apud animum suum decernat illum adoptare et optima haereditate donare, ita tamen ut non adeat hanc haereditatem priusquam ad annos pubertatis pervenerit, ac bonis literis et moribus excultus fuerit; vere dicamus hanc haereditatem tali personae consideratae ut indoctae, ut incultae, ut infanti, fuisse destinatam; at eadem haereditas tali personae consideratae ut excultae, ut doctae, ut puberi, fuit donata, idque ex destinato proposito adoptantis.
english: So whoever will receive eternal life was preconsidered by God as about to be faithful — antecedent to receiving eternal life — but not foreseen as already existing faithful — antecedent to destinating eternal life. Likeness: a man of good estate sees a wretched needy infant and at once decrees to adopt him and gift an excellent inheritance, yet not to enter it before puberty and cultivation in letters and manners. Truly that inheritance was destinated to him considered unlearned, uncultivated, an infant; yet the same inheritance was gifted to him considered cultivated, learned, of age — from the adopter's destinating purpose.

source_text: Si in aeternae haereditatis destinatione atque donatione simile quid cogitemus, facile praedicti argumenti infirmitatem perspiciemus. Plura non addo, quia idem pene argumentum, quamvis paululum immutatum, adductum fuit in Collatione Hagiensi, et a nobis antea refutatum.
english: Think the same pattern in destinating and gifting the eternal inheritance, and the weakness of their argument is plain. I add no more: nearly the same argument, slightly altered, was brought at the Hague Conference and already refuted by us.

source_text: Obj. 4. Si Deus praedestinaret quosdam ad vitam absque intuitu fidei antecedaneae, tum tales etiam servare vellet absque justitiae suae satisfactione; cum etiam tales magis diligeret, quam propriam suam justitiam: At haec falsa sunt: Ergo et illud unde consequuntur, scilicet, Deum praedestinare quenquam ante praevisionem fidei, quae satisfactionem Christi particularibus personis applicat ad salutem.
english: Obj. 4. If God predestinated some to life without intuition of antecedent faith, then he would also will to save them without satisfaction of his justice — loving them more than his own justice. But those are false. Therefore so is what follows from them: that God predestinates anyone before foresight of faith, which applies Christ's satisfaction to particular persons unto salvation.

source_text: Sol. Respondeo, Non concurrere ad voluntatem aeternam servandi in arcano electionis proposito inclusam, illa omnia quae concurrunt ad voluntatem servandi in ipso actu externo consummatam. Negamus igitur Majoris consequentiam, atque dicimus, Deum nunquam habuisse voluntatem servandi quenquam absque satisfactione justitiae suae; habuisse tamen voluntatem dandi quosdam Christo, dandi illis fidem per quam unio haec fieret, et per quam mediante hac fide Deo pro illis per Christi mortem efficaciter satisfaceret: atque haec omnia antecedenter ad praevisionem fidei ut in illis certe et infallibiliter existentis; non tamen absque praevisione, aut excludendo praevisionem fidei illis ex gratia Dei infallibiliter impertiendae.
english: Sol. I answer: not everything that concurs in the will to save as consummated in the external act also concurs in the eternal will to save enclosed in election's secret purpose. We deny the Major's consequence. God never had a will to save anyone without satisfaction of his justice; yet he had a will to give certain ones to Christ, to give them faith by which that union would be made, and by which, with that faith mediating, he would be efficaciously satisfied for them through Christ's death — all of this antecedent to foresight of faith as already certainly and infallibly existing in them, yet not without foresight, nor by excluding foresight of faith to be infallibly imparted to them from God's grace.

source_text: Fallere igitur nos conantur hujusmodi argumentationibus, dum illa absurda quae recte deducantur ab exclusa aut simpliciter negata praevisione fidei, illi deducunt a negata praevisione fidei secundum quid, hoc est, ut antecedanea conditione ad ipsam praedestinationem.
english: So they try to deceive us with such arguments: absurdities that follow only if foresight of faith is excluded or simply denied, they deduce from foresight denied secundum quid — that is, denied as an antecedent condition of predestination itself.

source_text: Obj. 5. Praedestinatio quae supponitur facta non ex praevisione fidei, pugnat cum natura vitae aeternae, et titulis quibus illa in Scripturis insignitur: Vocatur haereditas filiorum (at soli credentes sunt), merces, praemium, corona justitiae: Ergo non destinatur cuiquam citra omnem considerationem et intuitum fidei et obedientiae.
english: Obj. 5. Predestination supposed without foresight of faith fights the nature of eternal life and the titles Scripture gives it: inheritance of sons (but only believers are), wage, reward, crown of justice. Therefore it is destinated to no one apart from all consideration and intuition of faith and obedience.

source_text: Sol. Natura sive conditio vitae aeternae talis est, ut nemo in eam ingredi possit nisi qui antecedenter factus fuerit actu filius Dei per Spiritum adoptionis: at non est talis, ut nemo ad eam praedestinari possit nisi qui antecedenter fuerit filius Dei adoptatus. Praedestinatio enim continet propositum assumendi in filium: Tendit igitur in filium irae, quem praedestinando facit vas misericordiae quoad propositum; justificando, sanctificando, glorificando facit vas misericordiae quoad actum. Recte igitur requiritur fides antecedanea, aut saltem concomitans, ad constituendum filium actu adoptatum: at perperam requiritur fides antecedanea, ad constituendum Dei decretum de singulari persona adoptanda, et ad haereditatem destinanda.
english: Sol. Eternal life's nature is such that no one can enter it unless antecedently made actually a son of God by the Spirit of adoption — but not such that no one can be predestinated to it unless already an adopted son. Predestination contains the purpose of assuming into sonship: it tends on a child of wrath, whom by predestinatinating it makes a vessel of mercy as to purpose; by justifying, sanctifying, glorifying, a vessel of mercy as to act. Antecedent faith (or at least concomitant) is rightly required to constitute a son actually adopted; wrongly required to constitute God's decree about adopting a singular person and destinating the inheritance.

source_text: De titulis respondemus: Vitam aeternam dici mercedem, sive coronam fidei et obedientiae, sed ipsam praedestinationem ad vitam nunquam dici mercedem aut coronam sive fidei sive obedientiae nostrae. Vita aeterna dicitur merces fidei et bonorum operum quia credentibus et sancte viventibus ex promissione sive stipulatione Divina reddenda donatur: at beneficium praedestinationis nunquam sub ulla conditione fidei a nobis antecedente promissum ostenditur. Frustra igitur haec objiciuntur.
english: On the titles we reply: Scripture calls eternal life a wage or crown of faith and obedience — never predestination itself a wage or crown of our faith or obedience. Eternal life is that wage because God gifts it as something to be rendered, by promise or stipulation, to believers who live holy lives. Predestination as a benefit is never shown as promised under any condition of faith coming first from us. These objections therefore fail.

source_text: Obj. 6. Si electio non sit ex fide praevisa, tum Christus excluditur a decreto electionis, et homines sunt prius praedestinati ut serventur, quam Christus ut eos servet; nam qui nondum credunt, sunt adhuc extra Christum: Christus autem praedestinatus est Salvator fidelium solummodo, et sibi per fidem conjunctorum: Ergo praedestinatio est ex fide praevisa, aut Christus (quod nefas est) a decreto electionis excludetur.
english: Obj. 6. If election is not from foresight faith, then Christ is shut out of the election decree, and men are predestinated to be saved before Christ is predestinated to save them — for those who do not yet believe are still outside Christ. But Christ was predestinated Savior only of the faithful, joined to him by faith. Therefore predestination is from foresight faith, or Christ (which is impious) is shut out of the election decree.

source_text: Sol. Vacillat Majoris consequentia. Nam quamvis decretum electionis tendat in hominem mortuum ac in massa perditionis jacentem, ita tamen tendit, ut vitam ei non decernat nisi quatenus consideratur ut membrum, juxta Divinae voluntatis beneplacitum, Christo uniendum, et per Christum vivificandum. Atque hoc sensu, in Christo eliguntur qui nondum per fidem in Christum insiti considerantur.
english: Sol. The Major's consequence wobbles. The election decree does tend on a dead man lying in the mass of perdition — yet so that it decrees him life only as considered a member, by God's good pleasure, to be united to Christ and made alive through Christ. In that sense they are elected in Christ who are not yet considered grafted into Christ by faith.

source_text: Nam Caput Ecclesiae Christus ita conjunctus est cum membris suis omnibus, ut ipse prioritatem Causalitatis respectu reliquorum omnium obtineat, atque ut per et propter ipsum omnis boni gratuiti effluxus ad alios derivetur: derivatur autem non solummodo postquam sunt Christo insiti per fidem, sed ita ut hoc ipsum beneficium, quod per fidem illi inserendi destinantur, ab eo arcessendum sit, et in eo nobis conferendum. Quod igitur dicunt, Christum praedestinatum esse Salvatorem fidelium solummodo, id quidem verum est, quia non nisi per fidem omnes praedestinatos ad salutem perducit; non autem quia fides in omnibus praedestinatis ante ipsum decretum electionis invenitur.
english: Christ the Church's Head is so joined to all his members that he holds causal priority over all the rest, and every outflow of free good to others comes through and for him — not only after they are grafted into Christ by faith, but so that even the benefit of being destinated to be grafted by faith is fetched from him and conferred on us in him. That Christ was predestinated Savior of the faithful only is true — he leads all the predestinated to salvation only by faith — not because faith is found in all the predestinated before the election decree itself.

source_text: Addo denique, si electio esset ex fide praevisa, ut philosophatur Arminius, id absurdi revera sequeretur, quod nobis conatur impingere. Nam posita lege tali, Quisquis credet, ad vitam eligetur, manifestum est homines ne proposito quidem Divino in Christo existentes, sed extra Christum omnimode consideratos, credendo mereri, aut saltem ex pacto consequi, electionem suam. Tali autem electioni liberum uniuscujusque arbitrium fundamenti loco potius substernitur, quam Christus, quando ab universali lege ad actualem particularem hominum electionem descenditur.
english: Finally: if election were from foresight faith as Arminius philosophizes, the absurdity he tries to pin on us would truly follow. Posit the law Whoever believes will be elected to life — then men not even existing in the divine purpose in Christ, but considered wholly outside Christ, by believing merit or at least by pact obtain their election. Under that election each one's free choice is laid as foundation rather than Christ, when one descends from a universal law to the actual particular election of men.

source_text: Obj. 7. Si electio non ponatur ex antecedanea fidei praevisae conditione, tum Evangelium totum invertitur. Nam cum Evangelium prius mandet fidem, deinde sub conditione fidei salutem promittat, doctrina eorum qui Arminio repugnant, ponit Deum primo alicui personae singulari ordinasse salutem, deinde vero fidem. Evangelium dicit, Crede, et vives: haec vero doctrina dicit, Quoniam tibi volo dare vitam, propterea tibi volo dare fidem, quae est ipsissima Evangelii eversio. Concedenda ergo electio ex praevisae fidei conditione, aut Evangelii doctrina explodenda est.
english: Obj. 7. If election is not set from an antecedent condition of foresight faith, the whole Gospel is inverted. The Gospel first commands faith, then under that condition promises salvation — but those who resist Arminius have God first ordaining salvation to a singular person, then faith. The Gospel says, Believe and you will live; their doctrine says, Because I will to give you life, therefore I will to give you faith — the very overturning of the Gospel. So concede election from a foresight-faith condition, or explode Gospel doctrine.

source_text: Sol. Respondeo, Modo concedatur arcanum illud decretum Dei, cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult duritiae suae innatae relinquentes, Jacobum diligentis, Esavum odio habentis, idque ante omnem considerationem bene aut male factorum in iisdem, nos de ordine prioritatis et posterioritatis in decreto aeternae vitae et efficacis gratiae quoad ipsos praedestinatos, ne tantillum quidem laborare. Nam scimus in Deo quoad rem non esse decreta alia aliis priora aut posteriora: quoad modum autem considerationis nostrae et rerum inter se habitudinem idem decretum alteri comparatum potest eo et prius et posterius esse, secundum diversum ordinem causarum. Sic decretum dandi fidem in ordine causae efficientis prius est quam dandi vitam: decretum dandi vitam in ordine causae finalis prius est quam dandi fidem.
english: Sol. I answer: grant that secret decree of God who has mercy on whom he wills and leaves whom he wills to their innate hardness — loving Jacob, hating Esau, before any consideration of their good or evil deeds — and we do not labor even a little over priority and posteriority in the decree of eternal life and efficacious grace as to the predestinated. In God as to the thing, decrees are not prior or posterior to each other; as to our mode of considering and the mutual relation of things, the same decree compared to another can be both prior and posterior by a diverse order of causes. So the decree to give faith is prior in the order of efficient cause to giving life; the decree to give life is prior in the order of final cause to giving faith.

source_text: Recte enim Biel, Prius diligitur finis quam medium, quod propter finem diligitur: quia dilectio finis est aliquo modo causa dilectionis eorum omnium quae sunt ad finem. Cum enim fides sit donum Dei, vitam aeternam credenti apportans, quis audeat dicere hoc donum fuisse Petro aut Paulo praeparatum et donatum, vita aeterna nondum illis destinata? quasi Deus beneficium, quod ex suo dono orietur, non destinaverit ei, quem eodem dono prae aliis voluerit locupletare.
english: Biel is right: the end is loved before the means loved for the end's sake — love of the end is in some way cause of loving all that is unto the end. Since faith is God's gift bringing eternal life to the believer, who would dare say that gift was prepared and given to Peter or Paul while eternal life was not yet destinated to them? As if God had not destinated the benefit arising from his gift to the one he willed to enrich with that gift before others.

source_text: Sed accedamus propius ad rationem propositam. Negamus ex sententia nostra Evangelium inverti, aut quicquam Evangelio adversum in ea contineri. Evangelium dicit, Quisquis crediderit, salvus erit: Nos dicimus, Deum ex speciali misericordia quibusdam, quos infallibiliter ad vitam perducere decrevit, fidem constantem inspirare. Evangelium prius mandat fidem, deinde sub conditione fidei salutem promittit: Nos docemus, Deum primo ordinare singularem aliquam personam ad vitam, deinde vero fidem cordi ejusdem infundere. Ego pugnam aut contradictionem hic nullam invenio. Vox Evangelizantis instituit singulos, quibus modis et mediis possint vitam aeternam consequi: Media igitur sub conditione praemittit, quibus reis consecutionem promittit. At decretum Dei eligentis praestituit certis personis et media et finem, finem per media, et media propter finem; atque idcirco dicitur finem prius et principalius respicere, quia propter infallibilem ejus adeptionem talem gratiam concipitur tali personae praeparare.
english: Nearer then to their reason. We deny that our position inverts the Gospel or holds anything against it. The Gospel says Whoever believes will be saved; we say God from special mercy inspires constant faith in certain ones he has decreed to lead infallibly to life. The Gospel first commands faith, then under that condition promises salvation; we teach God first ordains a singular person to life, then pours faith into that heart. I find no fight or contradiction here. The evangelizing voice tells individuals by what means they may obtain eternal life — it puts means first under a condition and promises attainment to those who use them. But God's electing decree prefizes for certain persons both means and end — end through means, means for the end — and so is said to look to the end first and more principally, because for its infallible attainment such grace is conceived as prepared for that person.

source_text: Nullam hic contradictionem invenire potuit Augustinus, qui optime novit hanc esse Evangelii doctrinam, Quisquis ad finem usque perseveraverit, salvus erit; et tamen ipse docuit, Sanctis in regnum Dei ante jacta mundi fundamenta praedestinatis hanc ipsam perseverantiam praeparatam et donatam. Ut brevi absolvam; Nulla in hisce duobus effatis pugna est, Deus primo a nobis exigit officia fidei, deinde promittit beneficium vitae: et Deus, quoniam pro speciali sua misericordia quosdam elegit ad participandum vitae aeternae beneficium, propterea vult illis efficaciter fidem dare, ut impleant hoc officium.
english: Augustine found no contradiction here — he knew best that Gospel doctrine is Whoever perseveres to the end will be saved, yet taught that to saints predestinated into God's kingdom before the world's foundations this very perseverance was prepared and gifted. Briefly: these two sayings do not fight — God first exacts from us the duties of faith, then promises the benefit of life; and because for his special mercy he elected certain ones to share eternal life's benefit, he therefore wills to give them faith efficaciously so they may fulfill that duty.

source_text: Obj. 8. Qui secundum Dei voluntatem absque fide salvari non potest, non praedestinatur salvandus sine fide. Nulla est enim arcana Dei voluntas quae adversatur revelatae. Revelata dicit, Nolo Petrum salvare absque fide: Non est ergo arcana voluntas quae decernit eundem Petrum servare absque fide: ac proinde electio ad salutem est ex fide praevisa.
english: Obj. 8. Whoever by God's will cannot be saved without faith is not predestinated to be saved without faith. There is no secret will of God adverse to the revealed. The revealed says, I will not save Peter without faith — so there is no secret will decreeing to save that same Peter without faith. Therefore election unto salvation is from foresight faith.

source_text: Sol. Agnoscimus, adultorum neminem absque fide salvari posse, idque quia Divina voluntas ita ordinavit; quam voluntatis suae ordinationem in Evangelio patefecit et promulgavit. Concedimus etiam, neminem adultorum praedestinari salvandum sine fide. Sed hoc ambigue sumi potest; eget itaque distincta explicatione. Cum igitur praedestinare denotat actum internum in arcano mentis Divinae, Servare effectum externum in homine operatum: dicimus, neminem praedestinari salvandum absque fidei antecedentis consideratione, sub ratione medii ad productionem effectus illius externi: sed negamus, neminem praedestinari salvandum absque consideratione fidei antecedentis sub ratione motivi, ad productionem actus illius interni.
english: Sol. We grant no adult can be saved without faith — so God's will ordained, and he opened that ordination in the Gospel. We also grant no adult is predestinated to be saved without faith. But that can be taken ambiguously and needs distinct explanation. Predestinating denotes an internal act in the secret of the divine mind; Saving denotes an external effect wrought in the man. So: no one is predestinated to be saved without considering antecedent faith as a means to producing that external effect — but we deny that no one is predestinated to be saved without considering antecedent faith as a motive for producing that internal act.

source_text: Deus salvat per fidem, et Deus decernit servare per fidem; ita tamen ut fides intelligatur habere respectum causae vel conditionis antecedentis, non quoad ipsum decretum, sed quoad rem decretam. Effectus Divinae voluntatis potest procedere ex aliqua causa quam Deus ab aeterno praescivit, ipsumque ordinem causae ad causatum voluit: Et hoc dicitur causa voliti, non volendi.
english: God saves through faith, and decrees to save through faith — yet so that faith counts as an antecedent cause or condition not of the decree itself, but of the thing decreed. An effect of the divine will can proceed from a cause God foresaw from eternity and whose order to the caused he willed: that is called a cause of the thing willed, not of the willing.

source_text: Neque hac distinctione nostra collidimus arcanam voluntatem revelatae: Revelata siquidem dicit, Nolo Petrum salvare absque fide (scilicet praecedente, ut medio ad salutem ejus efficiendam ordinato): at revelata non dicit, Nolo Petrum servare absque fide praecedente tanquam motivo vel conditione ad formandum meum de ejusdem salute aeternum beneplacitum. Non igitur ex revelata Dei voluntate recte deducitur electio Petri ad salutem facta ex fide ejusdem antecedanea.
english: Nor does our distinction set the secret will against the revealed. The revealed does say, I will not save Peter without faith — namely preceding faith as a means ordained to effect his salvation. It does not say, I will not save Peter without preceding faith as a motive or condition for forming my eternal good pleasure about his salvation. So from the revealed will one cannot rightly deduce that Peter's election unto salvation was made from his antecedent faith.

source_text: Imo ex revelato Dei verbo recte deducitur, tum fidem, tum in fide perseverantiam ex praeeunte electione sive ad vitam ordinatione dependere. Huc spectant illa, Actor. xiii. 48. Crediderunt, quotquot ordinati erant ad vitam aeternam. Matth. xxiv. 24. Seductores in apostasiam pertraherent, si possibile esset, ipsos electos. Quod igitur quidam credunt, et quod credentes a fide non resiliunt, id ex antecedente electione dimanat: non, ut vult Arminius, quod quidem praevidentur credituri et in fide perseveraturi, exinde eorundem prae aliis electio dimanat. Plures ex Arminii scriptis objectiones non congeremus, quia hisce dissipatis, facile est et reliquas omnes, quae ejusdem farinae sunt, dissolvere. Veniemus igitur tandem ad defensionem nostram exponendam, et argumentis roborandam.
english: Indeed from God's revealed word it is rightly deduced that both faith and perseverance in faith depend on a preceding election or ordination unto life. So Acts 13:48 — as many as were ordained to eternal life believed — and Matt. 24:24 — seducers would draw even the elect into apostasy if it were possible. That some believe, and that believers do not spring back from faith, flows from antecedent election — not, as Arminius wills, that foresight of their believing and persevering is what makes their election flow before others. We will not heap more objections from Arminius's writings; these scattered, the rest of the same flour are easy to dissolve. We come at last to set out our defense and strengthen it with arguments.

source_text: Cap. VI. Orthodoxa sententia exponitur et confirmatur. Accepistis adversariorum argumenta pro illa electione, quam ex antecedaneo voluntatis humanae actu arcessunt. Restat ut nostra jam in medium proferantur, quae electionem sive praedestinationem singularium personarum ad infallibilem consecutionem vitae aeternae, ex mero Dei misericordiae beneplacito dimanare ostendent.
english: Cap. VI. The orthodox position is set out and confirmed. You have heard the adversaries' arguments for an election they fetch from an antecedent act of the human will. It remains to bring ours forward — showing that election or predestination of singular persons to the infallible attainment of eternal life flows from the mere good pleasure of God's mercy.

source_text: Neque tamen me latet Remonstrantes passim obtendere, electionem quam ipsi propugnant inniti sola gratia et misericordia Dei, non ullis meritis aut dignitate hominum. Verum cum totum discrimen electorum et non-electorum revocent ad praevisam fidem et infidelitatem eorundem, manifestum est id discriminis ad dignitatem et indignitatem hominum revocari. Nam fides Petri et perseverantia in fide habet in se moralem quandam dignitatem; sicuti incredulitas Judae et obstinatio in eadem, moralem indignitatem. Quod eo magis elucet, quia haec ipsa fides et perseverantia Petri non illi praeparata ex speciali aliquo Dei beneplacito, aut donata ex speciali aliqua munificentia, supponitur, sed oblata tantum in sufficienti mediorum administratione, sicuti etiam fuit illis qui increduli manserunt, a Petro autem per bonum usum liberi sui arbitrii acquisita et retenta; unde Petri electio est consecuta.
english: I am not unaware that Remonstrants everywhere claim the election they defend rests on God's grace and mercy alone, not on any human merits or dignity. But when they revoke the whole elect/non-elect discrimination to foresight of faith and unbelief, that discrimination is clearly revoked to human dignity and undignity. Peter's faith and perseverance have a certain moral dignity; Judas's unbelief and obstinacy a moral undignity. It shines the more because Peter's faith and perseverance are not supposed prepared by some special divine good pleasure or gifted by special munificence — only offered in a sufficient administration of means, as also to those who remained unbelieving — and acquired and kept by Peter through good use of free choice; whence his election followed.

source_text: Ex horum igitur sententia, si quaeratur, Cur hi crediderunt, illi non crediderunt? Cur hi perseveraverunt, illi non perseveraverunt? Cur hi ad vitam aeternam praedestinati fuerunt, illi non fuerunt? hae omnes quaestiones per humani arbitrii velle et nolle dissolvuntur. At juxta sententiam nostram est altius conscendendum, et licet humano arbitrio nequitiam et perditionem incredulorum tribuamus, tamen credentium fidem, perseverantiam, ipsamque ad vitam aeternam destinationem a speciali Dei beneplacito, atque speciali operatione eidem beneplacito respondente, petendam arbitramur. Neque hic necesse erit curiose disputare, utrum Deus vitam aeternam prius decernat electis, dein gratiam efficacem, an e contra: sed id solummodo agendum est, ut probetur singularibus quibusdam personis Deo soli notis et gratiam efficacem et gloriam praedestinari, praeparari ac donari.
english: On their view, ask why these believed and those did not, why these persevered and those did not, why these were predestinated to eternal life and those not — every question dissolves by human choice's willing and not-willing. On ours one must ascend higher: though we attribute unbelievers' wickedness and perdition to human choice, yet believers' faith, perseverance, and destination to eternal life are to be sought from God's special good pleasure and a special operation answering it. No need to dispute curiously whether God first decrees eternal life to the elect then efficacious grace, or the reverse — only to prove that to certain singular persons known to God alone both efficacious grace and glory are predestinated, prepared, and gifted.

source_text: Dicunt etenim et defendunt Remonstrantes, decretum praedestinationis sive electionis non cadere in quenquam, quem Deus non praevidit et consideravit ut credentem et ad extremum usque vitae habitum in fide perseverantem. Nos autem dicimus, praedestinationem antecedere hanc praevisionem; ita ut illi soli a Deo praevideantur et considerentur tanquam perseveranter credentes, quos Deus antecedente electionis suae proposito decrevit tales facere, factosque ad vitam aeternam perducere. Explodimus igitur illa Fausti Semipelagiani axiomata, quae non multum abludunt a mente et sententia Remonstrantium: qualia sunt; Salus hominum non in praedestinatione Factoris, sed in operatione famulantis collocata est. Non fuit specialis aliqua Dei munificentia erga credentes. Praedestinatis non est aliquorum bonorum causa. Praedestinatio ad justitiam pertinet. Nisi praescientia exploraverit, praedestinatio nihil decernit. Hisce omnibus opponimus hanc sententiam nostram; Praedestinationem singularium personarum ad vitam ex mero Dei beneplacito oriri, et non ex praevisis ullis humanae voluntatis operationibus: quin-etiam omnium bonarum operationum quae ad vitam aeternam ducunt, gratiam electionis causam antecedaneam ac fontem esse, non praemium aut mercedem sequentem. Argumentis jam agamus, ac ostendamus, merum Dei beneplacitum, non praevisam fidem ex una parte, et infidelitatem ex altera, facere primam discriminationem electorum et praeteritorum.
english: Remonstrants say and defend that the predestination or election decree falls on no one God has not foreseen and considered as believing and persevering in faith to life's last habit. We say predestination precedes that foresight — so only those are foreseen and considered by God as perseveringly believing whom God by the antecedent purpose of his election decreed to make such and, having made them, to lead to eternal life. We therefore explode Faustus the Semipelagian's axioms, not far from Remonstrant mind: Salvation of men is placed not in the Maker's predestination but in the servant's operation. There was no special divine munificence toward believers. Predestination is not cause of certain goods. Predestination pertains to justice. Unless foreknowledge has explored, predestination decrees nothing. Against all these we set ours: predestination of singular persons to life arises from God's mere good pleasure, not from any foresight operations of the human will — nay, of all good operations leading to eternal life, election's grace is the antecedent cause and fountain, not a following reward or wage. Now to arguments: mere divine good pleasure, not foresight faith on one side and unbelief on the other, makes the first discrimination of elect and passed-by.

source_text: Primum argumentum petetur a definitionibus Praedestinationis variis, definiente Augustino; Praedestinatio est praescientia et praeparatio beneficiorum Dei, quibus certissime liberantur quicunque liberantur. Ubi observandum, Deum praescire ea beneficia sive gratiae dona, quibus adhibitis ipse liberabit singulares quasdam personas electas; dein, haec omnia illis praeparare, ac tandem, sicut praescivit et praeparavit, opportuno tempore conferre. Quid hic cogitari potest, quod non dimanet a mero Dei beneplacito, omnem humanae voluntatis actum praecedente? Praescivit enim Deus in electis illa dona gratiae quae ipse illis praedestinavit et praeparavit secundum gratuitam suam benevolentiam, quando illos elegit in Christo. Ut aperte etiam ex Apostolo colligitur Ephes. i. 3–4. &c. Si quis hic, ut purae Dei misericordiae tenebras offundat, praevisam fidem obtendat fuisse causam, aut conditionem antecedaneam, nugas egerit; cum fides sit unum ex praecipuis hisce beneficiis quae in praedestinationis decreto praeparantur hominibus electis.
english: First argument: from various definitions of Predestination. Augustine: Predestination is the foresight and preparation of God's benefits, by which whoever are liberated are most certainly liberated. Observe: God foreknows those benefits or grace-gifts by which, applied, he will liberate certain singular elect persons; then prepares them all for them; and at length, as he foresaw and prepared, confers them at the right time. What here does not flow from God's mere good pleasure, preceding every act of the human will? He foresaw in the elect those grace-gifts he himself predestinated and prepared by free benevolence when he elected them in Christ — as Eph. 1:3–4 also openly shows. To cast darkness on pure divine mercy by putting foresight faith as cause or antecedent condition is trifling — faith is one of the chief benefits prepared for the elect in the predestination decree.

source_text: Sed missa Augustini definitione, audiamus ipsos Scholasticos. Aquinas dicit, Praedestinationem nil aliud esse quam praeparationem gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro. Hominem autem in massa corrupta, perdito, ne suspicari quidem possumus ei hanc gratiam et gloriam praeparari ex antecedente aliqua fidei perseverantis in eodem homine consideratione. Ridiculum est enim dicere, Deum homini decernere et praeparare illam gratiam, quam prius ut habitam et obtentam consideravit. Idem Aquinas alibi; Praedestinatio est quaedam ratio ordinis aliquorum in salutem aeternam in mente Divina existens. Atque mox subjungit, Exsecutionem hujus ordinis esse passive in praedestinatis, active autem in Deo. Si praedestinatio sit ordinatio quorundam in salutem, non debemus cogitare homines quosdam per fidem perseverantem prius ordinatos ad vitam, imo in ipso quasi vitae vestibulo positos, priusquam a Deo eligantur, aut praedestinentur. Sed ipsos Jesuitas defensionis nostrae hostes acerrimos audiamus. Sic igitur Vasquez, Praedestinatio est propositum aeternum Dei, quo gratiam alicui praeparat in vitam aeternam. Propositum praeparans gratiam quae ducit ad vitam aeternam infallibiliter, non potest ex praevisa hominum fide dependere, cum haec fides sit illa ipsa gratia de qua loquimur: Ad meram ergo Dei voluntatem referatur est necesse. Haec tam clara veritas extorsit Jesuitae ingenuam hanc confessionem, Discretio praedestinatorum a reprobis incipit ante consensum ipsorum absolute praevisum. ergo ante praevisam fidem, aut merita qualiacunque, quae sine consensu voluntatis humanae ne intelligi quidem possunt.
english: Passing Augustine's definition, hear the Scholastics. Aquinas: Predestination is nothing but preparation of grace now and glory hereafter. A man in the corrupt lost mass — we cannot even suspect that grace and glory are prepared for him from antecedent consideration of persevering faith in him. It is ridiculous to say God decrees and prepares for a man the grace he first considered as already had and obtained. Elsewhere Aquinas: Predestination is a certain reason of ordering some to eternal salvation existing in the divine mind — and the execution of that order is passively in the predestinated, actively in God. If predestination is an ordination of certain ones to salvation, we must not think some men by persevering faith first ordained to life — nay placed as it were in life's vestibule — before God elects or predestinates them. Hear even the Jesuits, fiercest enemies of our defense. Vasquez: Predestination is God's eternal purpose by which he prepares grace for someone unto eternal life. A purpose preparing grace that leads infallibly to eternal life cannot depend on foresight faith — that faith is the very grace in view — so it must be referred to God's mere will. That clear truth extorted this candid Jesuit confession: discrimination of predestinated from reprobate begins before their consent absolutely foreseen — therefore before foresight faith or any merits, which without human-will consent cannot even be understood.

source_text: Postremo audiatur ipse Arminius; Praedestinatio, inquit, est decretum beneplaciti Dei in Christo, quo apud se ab aeterno statuit fideles, quos fide donare decrevit, vita aeterna donare. Hic in praedestinatione duplex decretum involvitur: unum, Volo cunctis fidelibus dare vitam: alterum, Volo hisce certis personis dare fidem. Utrumque ex Dei gratuita et pura misericordia, neutrum ex praevisa fide aut aliqua humana operatione, dependet. Frustra igitur fidei praevisae conditionem praemittunt praedestinationi, quam omnes Theologi in ipsa praedestinationis definitione agnoscunt esse gratuitam, et fidei omnisque gratiae salutiferae scaturiginem. Atque haec sit prima nostra ratio, petita a communi consensu Theologorum in definienda ipsa Praedestinatione.
english: Finally hear Arminius himself: Predestination is God's good-pleasure decree in Christ by which from eternity he determined to gift eternal life to the faithful whom he decreed to gift with faith. Predestination involves a double decree: I will give life to all the faithful; and I will give faith to these certain persons. Both depend on God's free pure mercy — neither on foresight faith or any human operation. Vainly then they put a foresight-faith condition before predestination, which all theologians in defining predestination itself acknowledge as free, and the spring of faith and every saving grace. Let this be our first reason — from the common consent of theologians in defining Predestination itself.

source_text: Secundum argumentum desumetur a natura gratiae specialis liberantis, et de facto salutiferae. Nam ut recte observavit Augustinus, Praedestinatio non est gratiae cujuscunque, sed talis gratiae praeparatio: et talis gratia, nempe de facto salutifera, est praedestinationis effectus. Si igitur haec gratia in cordibus electorum fidem gignit, non invenit, tum multo magis ipsa electio, quae dandae talis gratiae causa fuit, pure gratuita esse debet, et ex nullo humanae voluntatis actu praeeunte, sed solummodo ex Divino beneplacito, pendere.
english: Second argument: from the nature of special liberating grace — grace that is in fact saving. As Augustine rightly observed, Predestination is not preparation of just any grace, but of such grace; and such grace, namely that which is in fact saving, is predestination's effect. If this grace in the elects' hearts begets faith rather than finds it, then much more election itself, the cause of giving such grace, must be purely free — depending on no preceding act of the human will, but only on the divine good pleasure.

source_text: Sic loquitur Apostolus, Servavit nos, et vocavit vocatione sancta, non ex operibus nostris, sed ex suo proposito et gratia. 2 Tim. i. 9. Haec gratia nullis malis meritis arcetur, nullis bonis impetratur, Prosper, ad Cap. Gallor. resp. 8. Haec gratia facit ut velimus, facit ut faciamus, facit ut credamus. Haec gratia bonas voluntates in hominibus operatur, Augustinus, De grat. Christi, cap. 29.
english: So Paul: he saved us and called us with a holy calling — not from our works, but from his purpose and grace (2 Tim. 1:9). Prosper (Response to the Gallican Chapters, 8): no evil merits bar this grace, no good ones purchase it. Augustine (On the Grace of Christ, ch. 29): it makes us will, makes us act, makes us believe, and works good wills in men.

source_text: Uno verbo, ut optime Augustinus, De bono persever. cap. 15. Haec gratia praevenit fidem, praevenit voluntatem, praevenit omnem obedientiam nostram; et haec omnia in eo cui datur, et cui haec omnia praevenit, operatur. Hisce omnibus ego addo, quod adversarii inficias ire non audebunt, talem gratiam dari a Deo ea intentione, ut haec omnia in electis et secundum propositum vocatis producat.
english: In a word, as Augustine best puts it (On the Gift of Perseverance, ch. 15): this grace goes before faith, before the will, before all our obedience — and works all these in the one to whom it is given and whom it thus goes before. Add what adversaries will not dare deny: God gives such grace with the intention that it produce all these in the elect and those called according to purpose.

source_text: Quandoquidem igitur haec specialis et efficax gratia quae fidem parit, et conversionem, non praerequirit antecedaneam fidei nostrae conditionem, sed datur quibusdam, aliis non datur, pro liberrima dantis aut non-dantis voluntate; manifestum est ipsam praedestinationem, quae est causa talis gratiae praeparatae et donatae, non esse alligatam actibus ullis antecedaneis humani arbitrii, sed constitutam in gratuito beneplacito ipsius Dei, juxta illud Apostoli, Miserebor cujus misertus fuero, Rom. ix. 15.
english: So this special efficacious grace that brings forth faith and conversion does not prerequire an antecedent condition of our faith — it is given to some and not to others by the freest will of the Giver. Plainly then predestination itself, the cause of such grace prepared and gifted, is not bound to any antecedent acts of human choice, but is constituted in God's free good pleasure — per Rom. 9:15, I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.

source_text: Tertio argumentamur ab auctoritate Scripturarum, tam affirmative quam negative, hoc modo. Scripturae Dei εὐδοκίαν sive beneplacitum causam praedestinationis nostrae passim commemorant; fidem autem praevisam nunquam sive causam, sive conditionem, sive antecedaneum praedestinationis statuunt. Ergo non oportet nos a puro beneplacito Dei ad fidem praevisam hoc ineffabile praedestinationis beneficium transferre. Huc faciunt illa Scripturae loca, Rom. ix. 11, Cum nihil fecissent boni vel mali, ut propositum Dei secundum electionem maneret; et Ephes. i. 11, In quo electi sumus, cum essemus praedestinati secundum propositum; et alia consimilia.
english: Third argument: from the authority of Scripture, both yes and no. Scripture everywhere names God's εὐδοκία — his good pleasure — as the cause of our predestination; it never sets foresighted faith down as cause, condition, or antecedent. So we must not shift this ineffable benefit off pure good pleasure onto foresighted faith. So Rom. 9:11 (when they had done nothing good or evil, that God's purpose according to election might stand) and Eph. 1:11 (chosen in him, predestined according to purpose) — and the like.

source_text: Jam e contra, adversarii ne unum quidem apicem ex Scripturis proferre possunt quo innuatur homines fuisse electos prae aliis ex praevisa antecedentis fidei in illis conditione. At si decretum praedestinandi praerequirat conditionem credendi, atque hac conditione impleta electio credentis consequatur, stipulatio haec ex sacris Scripturis est demonstranda. Nam fingere promissiones aut pacta extra verbum Dei est summae temeritatis. Quaero igitur, Ubi habetur haec promissio, Si credideris, praedestinaberis? Vel, Quicunque crediderint, praedestinabuntur? Extat promissio talis, Quisquis crediderit, salvabitur; quia Deus exigit conditionem fidei tanquam antecedaneum ad salutem decretam: At non extat haec, Quisquis crediderit, aut quisquis praevidetur crediturus, praedestinabitur; quia Deus non exigit fidem tanquam antecedaneum ad suum decretum.
english: On the other side, adversaries cannot produce so much as one tip of Scripture hinting that men were chosen above others from a foresighted condition of prior faith. If the predestining decree really presupposes believing, and election follows once that condition is met, that bargain must be shown from Holy Scripture — inventing promises outside God's word is sheer temerity. Where then is If you believe, you shall be predestined? Or Whoever believes shall be predestined? There is Whoever believes shall be saved — God requires faith as antecedent to decreed salvation. There is no Whoever believes (or is foreseen to believe) shall be predestined — God does not require faith as antecedent to his decree.

source_text: Sed respondentes Colloquutores Hagienses; Primo, se nunquam ponere praevisam fidem esse causam electionis, ac proinde non contravenire Scripturis, quae statuunt Dei εὐδοκίαν, vel solum beneplacitum esse ejus causam. Imo totidem verbis profitentur, causam, cur Deus singularem aliquam personam elegerit ad salutem, non esse fidem ejus, sed solum beneplacitum, gratiam, imo meram gratiam Dei. Sed haec omnia sunt mera verborum aucupia. Nam qui ponunt actum fidei perseverantis esse conditionem a Deo requisitam, ad cujus intuitum semper eligit, et ob cujus absentiam semper praeterit, ii vim causalem fidei adscribunt, imo meritoriam, eo sensu quo meriti vocabulum ab Augustino reliquisque Theologis in disceptationibus contra Pelagianos usurpatur. Sic Augustinus, Quis dicat illum qui jam coepit credere, ab illo in quem credidit nihil mereri?
english: The Hague Colloquy speakers answer first: they never call foresighted faith the cause of election, so they do not fight Scripture naming εὐδοκία — good pleasure alone — as cause. They even say outright that why God elects any one person to salvation is not that person's faith, but only good pleasure, grace, mere grace. Word-catching, all of it. Whoever makes persevering faith the condition God requires — at whose sight he always elects, and for whose absence he always passes by — gives faith causal force, even meritorious force, in Augustine's anti-Pelagian sense of merit. So Augustine: who would say that one who has already begun to believe merits nothing from him in whom he believed?

source_text: Nec Augustinus solummodo arguit beneficium illud ex merito dari, quod datur ex fidei conditione praeeunte, sed (quod notatu dignum est) quicunque olim electionem ad vitam ex conditione fidei suspenderunt, inde dignitatem et meritum antecedaneum in electis agnoverunt. Sic Prosper in Epist. ad Augustinum, ubi exponit sententiam illorum qui reliquiae Pelagianorum appellabantur: Quantum ad Deum pertinet, omnibus paratam vitam aeternam esse dicunt; quantum autem ad arbitrii libertatem, ab his eam apprehendi qui Deo sponte crediderint, et auxilium gratiae merito credulitatis acceperint. Sic etiam Hilarius ad Augustinum scribens de eadem materia, ostendit eos qui rejiciebant electionem secundum Dei propositum, et introducebant electionem secundum fidei et paenitentiae praevisionem, in hac fide et conversione meritum et causam electionis agnovisse: Eo merito quo voluerint et crediderint a suo morbo se posse sanari, etc. Et Paulo post, Si qualiscunque dolor oriatur, hanc ipsam dicunt causam propter quam alius assumatur, alius rejiciatur. Denique Faustus Regiensis, qui accuratissime Semipelagianorum sententiam tutatur, sicut electionem ex fide praevisa statuit, ita etiam ex merito eandem fieri non dissimulat: Praescientia, inquit, gerenda praenoscit, postmodum praedestinatio retribuenda describit; illa praevidet merita, haec praeordinat praemia. Nimis igitur arguti sunt, et a majoribus suis desciscunt Remonstrantes, quando ponunt Deum eligere homines secundum praescientiam fidei, et tamen negant fidem praevisam esse causam dictae electionis.
english: Augustine is not alone: whoever of old hung election to life on a faith-condition thereby admitted prior dignity and merit in the elect. Prosper (Letter to Augustine), on the so-called Pelagian remnants: as far as God goes, eternal life is prepared for all; as far as free choice goes, it is grasped by those who spontaneously believed, and received grace help by the merit of believing. Hilary to Augustine: those who rejected election according to God's purpose and brought in election by foresight of faith and penitence recognized in that faith and conversion the merit and cause of election — by the merit of willing and believing they can be healed, and later, whatever grief arises, they call that the very cause why one is taken and another rejected. Faustus of Riez, careful Semi-Pelagian: as he grounds election in foresighted faith, so he does not hide that it is also from merit — Foreknowledge knows what will be done; predestination then describes the retribution; the one foresees merits, the other preordains rewards. Remonstrants are too clever, and desert their elders, when they have God elect by foresight of faith and still deny that foresighted faith is the cause.

source_text: Secundo respondent, Etiamsi totidem verbis in Scripturis non reperiatur, Deum nos elegisse cum conditione si in illum credamus, ex eo tamen non posse concludi, Deum in electione non respexisse ad fidem. At regerimus, non modo totidem verbis, sed nullis aequipollentibus, nullis unde id recte deduci potest, hoc exprimi in Scriptura. Neque tamen negamus omnem respectum aut conditionem fidei in Deo eligente. Respicit enim et considerat fidem a se electis ingenerandam, tanquam medium quo pervenitur ad vitam: non respicit tanquam conditionem ab hominibus antecedenter praestitam aut praestandam, qua mediante pervenitur ad ipsam electionem.
english: Second reply: even if Scripture nowhere says in so many words that God elected us on condition we believe, you still cannot conclude he had no regard to faith in electing. We answer: not only is it missing totidem verbis — there are no equivalent words, nothing from which it can rightly be drawn. We do not deny every regard to faith in electing God. He regards the faith he will ingenerate in the elect as the medium by which one reaches life — not as a condition men have already performed or must perform in order to reach election itself.

source_text: Postremo dicunt Remonstrantes, nos errare, quando beneplacitum sive meram Dei gratiam et fidem praevisam in hoc negotio praedestinationis opponimus; quasi essent dicamus ex mera gratia et beneplacito, atque ex praevisa fide eligere; cum Apostolus ex eo quod haereditas sit ex fide, concludat eam esse ex gratia, Rom. iv. 16. Sed non est par ratio praedestinationis sive electionis obtinendae, et haereditatis regni caelestis adeundae. In negotio electionis esse ex fide, et esse ex mera gratia sunt ἐναντία, quia haec fides praesupponitur electioni, quae est ad primam gratiam, et scaturigo omnis gratiae salutiferae. At in causa adeundae vitae aeternae non sunt ἐναντία, quia haec fides est purae gratiae donum; et sic vitae praemium quod credenti redditur, est gratia pro gratia. Huc accedit, quod cum Deus humano generi proposuerit duplicem viam consequendae salutis, unam per opera Legis, Hoc fac, et vives; aliam per fidem Mediatoris, Crede, et salvus eris, recte dicitur ex gratia dari, quod datur ex fide; sicut ex operibus, quod datur ex Lege. Fuit enim gratiae Evangelicae singulare beneficium, relaxato foedere legali, salvare peccatores per fidem. At vero ex altera parte nunquam probabunt Remonstrantes Deum ordinasse duplicem modum praedestinandi homines: unum secundum opera, et alium secundum fidem. Si ergo quidam homines ex actu credendi ab illis praestito eligerentur, alii ob eundem actum omissum non eligerentur, discrimen hoc oriretur non ex speciali aliquo pacto aut actu gratiae Divinae, sed ex discriminatis actibus voluntatum humanarum. Esset enim praedestinatio Petri non ex speciali gratia Dei, sed ex speciali opere Petri: quia credere hic consideratur ut opus arbitrii per gratiam praeventi, oppositum contrario actui discredendi; non ut opus pacti alicujus Evangelici, oppositum pacto Legali, cum de praedestinatione talia pacta non exstent in utramvis partem.
english: Lastly Remonstrants say we err in opposing good pleasure (mere grace) to foresighted faith — as if electing from mere grace and from foresighted faith were rivals — since Paul, from inheritance being of faith, concludes it is of grace (Rom. 4:16). The cases are not alike. In election, of faith and of mere grace are ἐναντία: that faith is presupposed to election unto first grace, the spring of all saving grace. In entering eternal life they are not contraries: that faith is pure grace gift, so the life-reward rendered to the believer is grace for grace. God set the race a double path to salvation — Law: Do this and live; Mediator: Believe and be saved — so what comes by faith is rightly called grace, as what comes by Law is from works. Gospel grace singular gift, the legal covenant relaxed, is to save sinners by faith. Remonstrants will never prove God ordained a double mode of predestining — one by works, one by faith. If some were elected for a believing act they performed, and others passed over for omitting it, the split would come not from a special pact of divine grace but from differing human wills. Peter's predestination would then be from Peter's special work, not God's special grace: believing here counts as a work of grace-prevented choice against disbelieving — not as a Gospel-covenant work against the Legal, since no such covenants exist for predestination either way.

source_text: Quarto, disputamus a discrimine vocationis Divinae, quam ipsi Jesuitas atque Arminiani coguntur agnoscere. Sic autem instituitur haec ratio nostra: Si Deus quosdam vocat peculiari quadam vocatione (quam Apostolus, Rom. viii. 28, vocat vocationem secundum propositum; quam Prosper specialem vocationem, De vocat. Gent. 2. 23; Augustinus, vocationem qua fit credens, De Praed. Sanct. cap. 16, et vocationem secundum propositum, qua Deus implet quod praedestinavit, ibid. cap. 17, et gratiam occultam quae a nullo duro corde respuitur, ibid. cap. 8; quam denique ipsi Jesuitae vocationem congruentem et altam indigitant) — si inquam sit talis omnium electorum et non nisi electorum vocatio, tum clarum est Deum eosdem praedestinasse voluntate praevisam illorum fidem antecedente.
english: Fourth argument: from the difference of divine calling — which even Jesuits and Arminians must grant. If God calls some with a peculiar vocation (Paul's vocation according to purpose, Rom. 8:28; Prosper's special vocation; Augustine's vocation that makes a believer, and vocation according to purpose by which God fulfills what he predestined, and hidden grace no hard heart refuses; the Jesuits' congruent and high vocation) — if that calling is of all the elect and of none but the elect, then God clearly predestined them with a will that goes before any foresight of their faith.

source_text: Mediorum enim administratio respondet intentioni finis per eadem media obtinendi. Deus in hac vocatione electis, ac solis electis, administrat media quae novit fore infallibiliter efficacia, atque eo animo administrat, ut sint infallibiliter efficacia, idque ante omnem praevisionem fidei et conversionis in iisdem. Talia media preparari quibusdam ex mero Dei beneplacito, et non ex praevisa eorum fide, clarum est; quia infallibilis productio fidei et paenitentiae ex tali vocatione, tanquam effectus ex causa, consequitur. Si enim talia media hominibus quantumvis obduratis fuissent praeparata ac taliter administrata, illi etiam credidissent ac conversi fuissent.
english: Means answer the end they are meant to secure. In this vocation God gives the elect — and only the elect — means he knows will be infallibly efficacious, and gives them so that they will be, and that before any foresight of their faith or conversion. That such means are prepared for some from mere good pleasure, not foresighted faith, is plain: faith and penitence follow from such calling as effect from cause. Had the same means been so prepared and given even to the most hardened, they too would have believed and turned.

source_text: Sic Augustinus de praedestinatis et praeteritis disputans ex illo loco, Omnis qui audivit a Patre, et didicit, venit ad me, Joann. vi. 45: Hos omnes, inquit, docet venire ad Christum Deus, hos omnes vult salvos fieri, et in agnitionem veritatis venire. Nam si illos etiam, quibus stultitia est verbum Crucis, ut ad Christum venirent, docere voluisset, proculdubio venirent et ipsi. In hac igitur speciali vocatione agnoscamus necesse est specialem et antecedentem voluntatem salvandi sic vocatos.
english: So Augustine on the predestined and the passed-by, from John 6:45 (Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to me): all these God teaches to come to Christ; all these he wills saved and brought to the knowledge of the truth. Had he also willed to teach those for whom the Cross is foolishness to come to Christ, they too would have come. In this special vocation, then, we must grant a special antecedent will to save those so called.

source_text: De qua idem Augustinus: Deo volenti salvum facere nullum humanum resistit arbitrium; Deo volenti salvum facere sub conditione, Si homines velint credere, resistit arbitrium plurimorum: vult itaque quosdam salvos facere absoluto beneplacito praecurrente et causante eorum fidem, non praerequirente. Hujus rei consideratio eo adegit Arminium, ut fateretur, Deum non aequaliter omnium conversionem et salutem operari. At qui prudenter operatur, ex intentione finis dirigit ac gubernat modum suae operationis. Fuit ergo specialis voluntas et intentio salvandi quosdam ante eorum fidem praevisam, unde nascebatur illa specialis Dei vocatio et operatio, quae fidem in illorum cordibus gignebat. Quinetiam Vorstius, considerata hac speciali quorundam vocatione, concedit nobis exerceri erga quosdam extraordinariam quandam misericordiam, quae ab omni promissione libera et absoluta est: atque hujus respectu illud dici, Miserebitur quorum vult, Apud Piscat. in Resp. Apolog. pag. 17.
english: Augustine again: when God wills to save outright, no human will resists; when he wills to save only if men will believe, most wills resist — so he wills to save some by absolute good pleasure that goes before and causes their faith, not that presupposes it. That thought drove Arminius to admit God does not work everyone's conversion and salvation equally. But a prudent agent shapes his work from the end he intends. So there was a special will to save some before foresight of their faith — and from it sprang that special calling and working that begot faith in their hearts. Vorstius, weighing the same special vocation, grants that toward some God exercises an extraordinary mercy free of every promise and absolute — and in that sense, He will have mercy on whom he will (Piscator, Reply to the Apology, p. 17).

source_text: In summam redigo hanc rationem. Est quaedam vocatio specialis misericordiae, quae administratur hominibus quibusdam, non quia fuerunt considerati ut fideles, sed quia praedestinati ut fierent fideles. Haec vocatio fluxit ab antecedanea voluntate tales ad vitam aeternam infallibiliter destinante. Non omnium talis est vocatio, sed tantum electorum. Ergo electio ex beneplacito Dei non ex actu hominum dependet. Ergo est ad fidem, non ex fide. Nam hac vocatione voluntas cujusliber praedestinati, ut credat efficaciter, excitatur, etiam si tam sit aversus et ferox ut credentes persequatur, August. Contra 2. Epist. Pelag. lib. 1. cap. 19.
english: Sum: there is a special vocation of mercy given to some — not because they were already counted faithful, but because they were predestined to become faithful. It flows from an antecedent will that infallibly destines them to eternal life. Not everyone has that vocation — only the elect. So election hangs on God's good pleasure, not on human act. So it is unto faith, not from faith. By this calling every predestined will is stirred to believe efficaciously — even if so hostile and fierce that he persecutes believers (Augustine, Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 1.19).

source_text: Quinto, ab adjutorio inseparabili electionis sive praedestinationis probamus illam non ex fide nostra sed ex mero Dei beneplacito pendere. Nam electio importat certitudinem salutis quoad hominem electum, eamque non nudae scientiae (nam sic Deo ab omni aeternitate certissima sunt, quae sunt maxime fortuita) sed causalitatis, praedestinatione ita operante, ut certo perducat praedestinatum ad vitam aeternam.
english: Fifth argument: from election's inseparable help — it hangs not on our faith but on God's mere good pleasure. Election means certainty of salvation for the elect person: not bare knowledge (even the most chance events are utterly certain to God from eternity) but causality — predestination so working that it surely leads the predestined to eternal life.

source_text: Unde illud Matth. xxiv. Adeo ut seducant, si fieri posset, etiam electos. Et Rom. xi. 5. Reservatio secundum electionem. Et Ephes. i. 11. Cum essemus praedestinati secundum propositum ejus qui omnia efficit ex consilio voluntatis suae. Quoad Deum igitur certa est salus electorum; quia ex decreto electionis statuit miris modis ita agere in cordibus eorum ut perducantur ad fidem et paenitentiam, ut in fide et vitae novitate permaneant, ac tandem moriantur in Domino.
english: Hence Matt. 24 (to deceive, if possible, even the elect), Rom. 11:5 (a remnant according to election), and Eph. 1:11 (predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things by the counsel of his will). Quoad God, the elect's salvation is certain: from the election decree he has resolved so to work in their hearts that they are led to faith and penitence, remain in faith and newness of life, and at last die in the Lord.

source_text: At in illa Praedestinatione Arminiana, ubi fides praevisa post se trahit electionem, nulla est certitudo salutis ex Deo specialiter causante, sed solummodo ex Deo intuente. Nam in quatuor Arminii decretis, quibus praedestinationis naturam describit, nullum est quod certitudinem salutis singulari alicui personae apportet, per modum causae infallibiliter operantis; sed salutem electorum Deo certam relinquit per modum intuentis.
english: In Arminian predestination, where foresighted faith drags election after it, there is no certainty of salvation from God as special cause — only from God as onlooker. Of Arminius's four decrees describing predestination, none gives any singular person certainty of salvation by an infallibly operating cause; elect salvation stays certain to God only as one who sees.

source_text: Primo, ponit decretum de dando Mediatore. Secundo, adjungit aliud, de salvandis credentibus et perseverantibus propter hunc Mediatorem. Tertio, de administrandis mediis ad fidem necessariis. Quarto, de salvandis illis quos praevidet beneficio horum mediorum crediturus et perseveraturos. In tribus prioribus manifestum est nullam certitudinem salutis singulari personae causari; quia communia sunt, et aeque ad reprobos atque electos spectare possunt, quoad nudam decretorum formam.
english: First: a decree to give a Mediator. Second: to save believers and perseverers for that Mediator's sake. Third: to administer the means needed for faith. Fourth: to save those he foresees will believe and persevere by those means. The first three cause no certainty of salvation for any one person — they are common, and in bare form can as well cover reprobates as elect.

source_text: Quartum vero decretum, quod solum de singularibus personis agit, certitudinem salutis non affert per modum causae operantis, sed per modum scientiae praevidentis: quia Deus ibi non statuit fidem et perseverantiam in electis efficaciter producere, sed eosdem tanquam jam credituros et perseveraturos intueri. Ubi igitur nulla est certitudo salutis ex Deo specialiter et infallibiliter causante, ibi non est vera illa electio Scripturis celebrata. Ergo electio pendet ex mero Dei beneplacito, non ex fide praevisa.
english: The fourth decree alone touches singular persons — and even it gives certainty only as foreseeing knowledge, not as an operating cause: God does not there resolve to produce faith and perseverance in the elect, but only to regard them as already about to believe and persevere. Where salvation is not certain from God specially and infallibly causing, there is not the election Scripture celebrates. So election hangs on mere good pleasure, not foresighted faith.

source_text: Septimo, argumentamur ab inconveniente vel absurdo, quo laborat haec eorum sententia qui suspendunt actum electionis Divinae ex praeeunte actu fidei ac perseverantiae humanae. Hinc enim sequeretur, nec formalem nec materialem numerum electorum esse certum ac definitum secundum decretum aliquod beneplaciti Divini, sed quod hae singulares personae, et hoc definito numero, salventur, id per accidens evenisse, ex contingente nimirum actu arbitrii humani, Deo praevidente, non praeordinante.
english: Seventh argument: from the absurdity their view labors under — hanging divine election on a prior act of human faith and perseverance. Then neither the formal nor the material number of the elect would be fixed by any decree of divine good pleasure; that these particular persons are saved, and in this fixed count, would be an accident of contingent human choice — God foreseeing, not preordaining.

source_text: Antiqui Semipelagiani viderunt hoc necessario sequi ex praedicta sententia, atque idcirco tanquam nihil absurdi in se haberet, hoc palam docuerunt. Sic Faustus De lib. arbit. lib. 1. Status hominis in diversa, non pro constitutione Dei, sed pro arbitrii libertate potest versari. Et libro 1. cap. 20. Quid de nobis praescire ac praeordinare debeat Deus, quantum pertinet ad futurum, in profectu hominis defectuque consistit.
english: The old Semi-Pelagians saw that sequitur and taught it openly as no absurdity. Faustus (On Free Choice 1): a man's state can turn this way or that not by God's constitution but by free choice. And 1.20: what God is to foreknow and preordain about us for the future consists in man's progress or failure.

source_text: Multo autem apertius id asseruerunt Pelagianorum reliqui, apud Prosperum et Hilarium in Epistolis ad Augustinum. Sic igitur Prosper: Non acquiescunt praedestinationi, electorum numerum nec augeri posse nec minui. Et Hilarius: Hi non recipiunt, ut eligendorum et rejiciendorum esse definitum numerum velint.
english: The Pelagian remnants said it more openly still — Prosper and Hilary in their letters to Augustine. Prosper: they will not grant predestination that the elect's number can neither grow nor shrink. Hilary: they will not have a defined number of those to be chosen and rejected.

source_text: Atque ex nuperis Jesuitis Lessius, qui magis aperte hanc causam egit, confidenter asserit, De completa praedestinatione nullam aut raram esse mentionem in Scripturis, quia haec non pendet ex nudo Dei beneplacito, sed ex perseverantia humana. Quinetiam docet, Intentionem Dei de numero salvandorum non fuisse absolutam ante praevisionem finis mundi.
english: Among recent Jesuits, Lessius presses it more openly: Scripture barely mentions complete predestination, he says, because it hangs not on bare good pleasure but on human perseverance. He even teaches that God's intention for the number of the saved was not absolute before foresight of the world's end.

source_text: Haec si ita essent, nulla esset differentia inter electos et praeteritos ex Divina operatione, sed solummodo ex humana; nec Petrus a Deo magis ordinatus ad vitam aeternam fuisset quam Judas: sed quia credendo et perseverando satisfecit universali huic decreto, Quisquis perseveranter crediderit, salvus erit, Judas autem non satisfecit, ideo fuit hic in electorum numerum receptus, iste ab eodem numero exclusus. Sed haec omnia sunt plane absurda et cum Scripturis pugnantia, quae docent quosdam in Christo electos ante jacta mundi fundamenta, ut essent sancti et inculpati, Eph. i. 4. Quosdam prae aliis fide donatos, quia prae aliis fuerunt a Deo ex mera misericordia ad vitam ordinati; ut Matth. xi. 25, 26; Act. xiii. 48; Joh. vi. 37; et alibi passim.
english: If so, elect and passed-by would differ only by human operation, not divine — and Peter would be no more ordained by God to eternal life than Judas. Peter would enter the elect number only because he met the universal decree Whoever perseveringly believes shall be saved; Judas failed it and was shut out. Plainly absurd, and at war with Scripture: some elected in Christ before the world's foundation, to be holy and blameless (Eph. 1:4); some gifted with faith before others because before others God from mere mercy ordained them to life — Matt. 11:25-26; Acts 13:48; John 6:37; and throughout.

source_text: Octavo, sic argumentamur. Nemo unquam praevisus est ut habens fidem perseverantem, cui Deus nondum decrevit hoc eximium donum impertire. Quod si Deus jam decreverit Petro, Paulo, aut cuilibet homini singulari dare perseverantiam; manifestum est illum jam esse a Deo ad vitam electum et ordinatum. Nam in ipso perseverantiae dono sita est infallibilis ad vitam aeternam ordinatio. Parum igitur rationi consentaneum est, ipsum Deum eligere singulares personas ad vitam ex praevisione proprii sui doni, quod nunquam dedit, aut dare decrevit, nisi illis quos antecedenter ad vitam aeternam destinavit.
english: Eighth argument: no one was ever foreseen as having persevering faith unless God had already decreed to give that excellent gift. If God has decreed perseverance for Peter, Paul, or any particular person, that one is already elected and ordained to life — for the gift of perseverance itself carries an infallible ordination to eternal life. It is hardly reasonable that God should elect particular persons to life by foresight of his own gift, which he never gives or decrees to give except to those he has already destined to eternal life.

source_text: Nihil video in hoc argumento quod ullo modo possit labefactari aut in dubium vocari. Nam primo, si quis diceret fidem perseverantem posse in aliquibus praevideri quibus Deus hanc perseverantiam nondum decreverit donare, ille tantum bonum ab humano arbitrio, non a Divino munere arcesseret. At tota Scriptura reclamat, quae perseverantiam sanctorum ex dono Dei ostendit dimanare: Reverentiam mei indam animo ipsorum, ut non recedant a me, Jer. xxxii. 40. 2 Thess. iii. 3. Fidelis est Deus, qui stabiliet vos et tuebitur a malo. Et Augustinus secundum Scripturas clare docuit, hanc perseverandi possibilitatem et voluntatem Divinae gratiae largitate donari sanctis in regnum Dei praedestinatis, aliis non donari. Est ergo verissimum illud Aquinatis: Voluntas Dei qua vult hoc bonum alicui diligendo, est causa quod illud bonum ab eo prae aliis habeatur, Part. 1. qu. 23. art. 4.
english: Nothing here can be shaken. First: if persevering faith could be foreseen in those to whom God has not yet decreed perseverance, that great good would come from human choice, not God's gift. All Scripture protests — saints' perseverance flows from God's gift: I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not depart from me (Jer. 32:40); Faithful is God, who will establish you and keep you from evil (2 Thess. 3:3). Augustine, following Scripture, taught that the power and will to persevere is given by grace's largess to saints predestined into God's kingdom — and not to others. So Aquinas is right: God's loving will that someone have this good is why he has it before others (ST 1.23.4).

source_text: Secundo, perseverantiam non donari aut destinari nisi ad vitam aeternam electo et destinato, inde clarum est, quod ab agente qui vim et efficaciam mediorum intelligit, media ad finem consequendum infallibiliter efficacia nunquam praeparantur et donantur cuiquam nisi ex proposito et desiderio finis. Huc spectant illa Petri verba, virtute Dei custodimini per fidem ad salutem, 1 Petr. i. 5. Deus inspirat fidem cordibus nostris, inspiratam custodit ne exstinguatur, atque idcirco hoc facit, ut per fidem perducamur ad salutem. Salus igitur eorum omnium fuit apud Deum certissima, quibus fidem perseverantem dare decrevit.
english: Second: perseverance is given only to one already elected and destined to eternal life. An agent who knows what means can do never prepares and gives infallibly efficacious means except from purpose and desire of the end. So Peter: by God's power you are kept through faith unto salvation (1 Pet. 1:5). God inspires faith, keeps it from going out, and does so that through faith we may be led to salvation. All to whom he decreed persevering faith had salvation most certain with God.

source_text: Hoc argumentum valde torquet tam Arminianos quam Jesuitas. Arminiani itaque non ausint aperte negare, fidem perseverantem esse donum Dei, tamen strenue negant, actionem eam per quam Deus nobis fidem donat, semper efficacem, certam, et invictam esse. Atque porro docent, quando Deus dat hominibus potentiam ad ipsum perveniendi, fidem jam esse iisdem paratam ut donum, modo continuetur haec gratia. Proculdubio idem sentiunt de perseverantia, nempe hoc dono nil aliud designari quam illam sufficientem gratiam, qua datur hominibus potentia perseverandi si velint. Tale autem donum non arguit praeeuntem destinationem ad vitam aeternam; quia hoc modo fides et perseverantia donatur illis, qui nec fidem, nec perseverantiam, nec vitam aeternam unquam habuerunt aut habituri sunt.
english: This argument badly torments Arminians and Jesuits alike. Arminians dare not openly deny that persevering faith is God's gift — yet they strongly deny that the act by which God gives faith is always efficacious, certain, and invincible. They teach that when God gives men power to reach him, faith is already prepared as a gift if that grace continues. Doubtless they hold the same of perseverance: the 'gift' means only sufficient grace — power to persevere if they will. That kind of gift does not imply prior destination to eternal life; it is 'given' even to those who never had and never will have faith, perseverance, or eternal life.

source_text: Sed haec parum coherent aut inter se aut cum Scripturis. Non inter se; quia fides aut perseverantia data singulari personae ex parte Dei, innuit obtentam et habitam ex parte hominis. Quaedam enim dona ejusmodi sunt, ut involvant ipsam receptionem, absque qua ne intelligi quidem possunt esse donata. Tale donum est bona voluntas credentis et perseverantis, quae nunquam fuit a Deo data ulli homini a quo non fuit accepta. Non enim quaeritur de dono parato et offerendo, atque sub conditione contingente dando certis personis, aut non dando, sed de dono certis personis vere et actualiter donato. Porro, cum Scripturis pugnat Arminiana illa fidei ac perseverantiae donatae interpretatio. Nam Scripturae dicunt fidem iis donatam quibus datum est ipsum credere, non quibus datum est solummodo ut possint credere, Phil. i. 29. Perseverantiam etiam illis datam pronunciant, non qui potuerunt perseverare et resilierunt, sed qui Divino munere ita corroborati et sustentati fuerint, ut ipso facto perseveraverint. Late hoc probat Augustinus, De Corr. et grat. cap. 11, 12. Ubi ostendit, dari jam omnibus praedestinatis in Christo, quod non fuit datum Adamo; nempe tale adjutorium, ut per illud non solummodo perseverare possint si velint, sed etiam ut velint, et reapse perseverent.
english: This coheres neither with itself nor with Scripture. A faith or perseverance God gives to a particular person implies it is had on man's side. Some gifts include the reception itself — without reception they cannot even be understood as given. The good will of the believer and perseverer is such a gift: God never gave it to anyone who did not receive it. The question is not a gift prepared and offered under a contingent condition, but a gift truly and actually given to certain persons. Arminian reading fights Scripture: faith is given to those to whom it is given to believe — not merely to be able to believe (Phil. 1:29). Perseverance is pronounced given not to those who could have persevered and sprang back, but to those so strengthened by God's gift that they actually persevered. Augustine at length (On Rebuke and Grace 11–12): all predestined in Christ receive what Adam did not — help such that they not only can persevere if they will, but will, and in fact persevere.

source_text: Ab hoc dono, quibusdam specialiter praeparato et donato, nos colligimus, vitam aeternam fuisse iisdem antecedenter destinatam. Vasques Jesuita convictus de absoluta hac et gratuita certarum personarum ad fidem et perseverantiam praedestinatione, respondet, esse verissimum, praedestinationem ad habendam gratiam non dependere ex praevisis meritis aut actionibus nostris; sed electionem ad habendam gloriam ex illis dependere, atque hanc esse perpetuam Scripturarum et Augustini sententiam. Sed frustra conatur Jesuita divellere, quae Scriptura et Augustinus optimus hac in re Scripturarum interpres, docuit esse conjunctissima. Scriptura enim non agnoscit aliam electionem aut praedestinationem ad gratiam efficacem, quam quae connexa est cum ea voluntate dandi gloriam; quae voluntas, secundum nostrum considerandi modum, prior est voluntate dandi gratiam efficacem, et causa ac regula ejusdem. Hinc praedestinati dicimur in adoptionem filiorum, Ephes. i. 5. quae non modo gratiae, sed gloriae sive haereditatis caelestis destinationem perspicue denotat. Sic Christus loquens de praedestinatis, Luc. xii. 32. Nolite, inquit, timere, pusille grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Ubi voluntas dandi regnum affertur tanquam causa peculiaris ejus providentiae quam Deus exercet erga electos, ut eos custodiat, et non obstantibus periculis et tentationibus perseverare faciat. Voluntas ergo dandi gloriam, sive electio ad vitam, est ratio cur prae aliis perseverent; non praevisa perseverantia, ratio cur prae aliis electi fuerint.
english: From this gift specially prepared and given to some, we gather eternal life was already destined for them.
